RESOLUTION No. 1.

A RESOLUTION providing for the holding of a General Municipal Election in the
* City of Los Angeles, on the first Monday of December, A. D. 1878.

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, as follows:

Srcrion 1. That a General Municipal Election be held by the qualified voters
of the City of Los Angeles, in said city, on the first Monday of December, A. D.
1878, the same being the second day of said month, for the following officers, to-wit:

A Mayor,

A Tax Collector,

A City Attorney,

A City Treasurer,

A City Assessor,

Three members of the Board of Education of said city;

Also, by the qualified voters of the respective wards of said city, for members of
the Council of said city, that is to say:—three members of the* Council to represent
the First Ward, three members of the Council to represent the Second Ward, three
members of the.Council to represent the Third Ward, three members of the Council
to represent the Fourth Ward, three members of the Council to represent the Fifth
Ward.

The polling places shall be as follows:
For First Ward—In a room on the floor of Benner’s building (so called), opposite

the Southern Pacific Railroad depot, on Alameda street, near Mission street.
For Second Ward—In the Assessor’s room, at the Court House in said city.
For Third Ward—At Turnverein Hall, on Spring street, between Second and

Third streets. ;
For Fourth Ward—At Santa Monica depot (so called), on San Pedro street, in

said city.
For Fifth Ward—In the barroom of D. V. Waldron, at Washington Gardens, on
Washington street, in said city.

ORDINANCE No. 1.

An ORDINANCE providing for the sale of water for irrigating purposes in the winter
season.
The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Secrion 1. That from the first day of November, 1878, to the first day of
March, 1879, water shall be furnished and sold to irrigators on the following terms
and none others, to-wit:

For water used inside the city limits:—For one head, one dollar per day; for
one night, fifty cents.

For outside the city limits:—Two dollars per day, and one dollar per night.

Szc. 2. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordinance,
and cause the same to be published once in English in the Los Angeles Dainty
Eveninc Express, and once in Spanish in La Cronica, and thereupon and
thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

-L hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles, at its session of December 26th, 1878.
W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

RESOLUTION No. 4.

A RxsoLution of the Council of the City of Los Angeles, fixing the salaries of the
several officers of said city.

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, as follows:

Section 1. That from and after the first day of January, 1879, there be al-
lowed and paid, as hereinafter stated, to the several officers named, the following
sums in lawful money of the United States, as salaries:

To the Chief of Police, one hundred and twenty-five dollars per month.

To the City Auditor and ex-officio Clerk of the Council, one hundred and fifty
dollars per month.

To the City Zanjero, ninety dollars per month.

To each deputy Zanjero employed between the first day of March and the first
day of October of the same year, compensation at the rate of seventy-five dollars
per month.

To each foot Policeman, eighty dollars per month.

To each horse or mounted Policeman, ninety dollars per month.

To each special Policeman, such sum per day as the Council shall from time to
time by order entered on its minutes, determine. |

To the Health Officer, seventy-five dollars per month.

To each Engineer of the fire companies, one hundred dollars per month.

To each Driver of the fire companies, seventy-five dollars per month.


===== PDF PAGE 7 = PRINTED PAGE 7 =====
OF THE CITY OF ‘LOS ANGELES. 7

To the City Sexton, twenty-two 50-100 dollars per month.

To the City Surveyor, one hundred dollars per month.

‘To the City Assessor, for services rendered in the collection of taxes on personal
property, four per cent. on the amount collected.

To the Overseer of the chain-gang, seventy-five dollars per month.

The salaries herein named to be paid monthly, are to be paid at the end of
each and every month, and for that purpose, the Clerk of the Council and the
Mayor of the city are hereby authorized and directed at the end of each and every
month, to draw and sign warrants on the salary fund in favor of such officers re-
spectively, for the several amounts due them.

The above resolution was presented to the Mayor for his approval December
3lst, A. D. 1878, and returned by him to the Clerk of the Council without his
approval on January 17th, A. D. 1879. By reason of not being returned within

ORDINANCE NO. 2.

An Orvrinance prohibiting the sales at auction, on the public streets of the City of
Los Angeles.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. All persons are hereby prohibited from selling horses, mules, hogs,
jacks, jennies, horned cattle, sheep, goats, or other live stock, or wares and mer-
' chandise, or articles of any description, at auction, in any of the public streets, or
on any of the sidewalks of the City of Los Angeles.

Sec. 2. Any person violating any of the provisions of this ordinance shall be
deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and on conviction shall be punished by a fine not
exceeding two hundred dollars, or imprisonment not exceeding six months, or both.

Sec. 3. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordinance,
and shall cause the same to be published once in English in the Los Angeles Daily
Eventne Express, and once in Spanish in La Cronica, and thereupon and there- '
after it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council at its
session of the 16th January, 1879.
W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council.
Approved this 24th day of January, A. D. 1879.
J. R. TOBERMAN,

Mayor.
Published February 18th, 1879.

A ResoLurtion defining the fire limits of the City of Los Angeles.
Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, as follows:

SEction 1. That section 3 of a resolution of the Common Council of the City of
Los Angeles, to provide for the protection of persons and property in said city from
damages by fire, adopted May 7, 1874, as amended by resolution of said Council,
adopted March 8, 1877, is hereby repealed, and section 3 of said resolution, adopted
May 7, 1874, shall hereafter read as follows: Section 3.—The boundaries ef the
respective districts shall be as follows, to-wit: Beginning at a point in the center
of the intersection of First and Fort streets; thence easterly along the center of
First street to the center of Wilmington street; thence northerly along the center of
Wilmington street to the center of Commercial street; thence easterly along the
center of Commercial street to the center of Alameda street; thence northerly along
the center of Alameda street to Marchessault street; thence westerly along the center
of Marchessault street to the center of New High street; thence southerly along the
eenter of New High street to the center of Temple street; thence westerly along the
center of Temple street to the center of Fort street; thence southerly along the
center of Fort street to the place of beginning.

Sc. 2. All ordinances and resolutions conflicting herewith are hereby repealed.

Src. 8. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this resolution,

ORDINANCE No. 3.

|
AN ORDINANCE to provide for the licensing of business carried on in the City of
Los Angeles.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

Section 1. It shall be unlawful for any person or persons to conduct or carry
on within the corporate limits of the City of Los Angeles, any vocation, trade, call-
ing or employment in this ordinance specified, either in their own names and for
their own profits and benefit, or as agents for any other person or persons, or' body
corporate, or otherwise, without first procuring from said city a license so to do; and
if sueh person or persons, either for themselves or as agents, shall conduct or carry
on any vocation, trade, calling, business or employment aforesaid, without having
procured such license, he, she, or they, for each violation of this ordinance, shall be
deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and, upon conviction by any court having jurisdic-
tion thereof, shall be fined therefor, in a sum not less than ten nor more than two
hundred dollars, or shall be imprisoned for a term*not exceeding ninety days, or
both, and the amount of said license shall be deemed a debt due to the said City of |
Los Angeles, and all such persons, bodies, corporate and their agents, or either of
them, shall, for each and every violation of this ordinance, be liable to an action in
the name of the City of Los Angeles, in any court of competent jurisdiction, for the
amount of the monthly license of such business as he or they may be engaged ‘in,
with costs of suit.

Src. 2. That the monthly rates of license for the pursuits, business, trades,
occupations, avocations and employments hereinafter named be, and the same are
hereby established for and within the City of Los Angeles, and the same shall be
paid by the owners or proprietors thereof, as follows, that is to say:

For the business of banker, where the capital stock exceeds three hundred
thousand dollars, $30; where the capital stock amounts to two hundred thousand
dollars, and is less than three hundred thousand dollars, $25; where the capital
stock amounts to less than two hundred thousand dollars, $20. 5

For every money broker, $5.

For every butcher shop or stall whose monthly sales exceed $400, $3.

For every butcher shop or stall whose monthly sales are under $400, $2.

For every person who, having no butcher shop or stall, engages in the business
of selling meat inside the city limits, $3; provided, however, that this shall not
apply to occasional sales of meat by persons not engaged in the sale of the same as a
business.

For every undertaker, $10.

For every cheap-John stand, $15.

For every prize-picture lottery, $25.

Por carrying on, manufacturing and selling gas, $25.

For all persons or corporations not municipal, vending water for domestic
purposes, where the monthly sales do not exceed five hundred dollars, $5; where the
monthly sales exceed five hundred and do not exceed one thousand dollars, $15;
for all exceeding one thousand dollars, $25.

For all manufacturers of ice whose monthly sales exceed $100, $5.

license of $3 per month.

Every person conducting or carrying on the regular business of selling fruit on
stands fronting on the public streets, or upon wagons or vehicles standing in the
public streets, shall pay a monthly license of $1.

No person shall conduct or carry on in the public streets any business heretofore
mentioned; either from stands or wagons or other vehicles, without first having
obtained the consent of the owner or owners of the property fronting on that portion
of the public streets where such stand or vehicle may be located, whether he shall
have obtained said license or not, and any person carrying on said business without
said consent shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and each and every day he
shall carry on said business, shall constitute a new and separate offense, and shall be
punished accordingly.

Every person conducting or carrying on as a general or regular means of
livelihood the trade, calling or business of peddling in a wagon upon the streets of
said city, any kind of vegetables, shall pay a license per month of $12.

Each soda-water factory shall pay a license of $2.50.

Each storehouse for grain of capacity of 500 tons or more, shall pay a license of $3.

Each storehouse for grain of capacity less than 500 tons, shall pay a license of $2.

Each milkman whose sales per month average over one hundred dollars and less
than four hundred dollars per wagon, for each wagon, $2.

Each milkman whose sales per month average four hundred dollars or more per
wagon, for each wagon, $4.

Suc. 3. The licenses in this ordinance provided for, shall be due and payable to

the city on the first Monday of each month in advance, excepting where said license
is per day, when the same shall be paid each day in advance; and where said license


===== PDF PAGE 15 = PRINTED PAGE 15 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. ~~ 15

is per annum, the same shall be paid at the time specified in the ordinance providing
the same, and, when not so specified, in the month of December of each year,

The Tax Collector of said city shall deliver the books in ‘his office containing a
report of the names of all persons from whom licenses are now collected; and also,
on or before the 25th day of each month, he shall deliver to, the Clerk of the Council
the delinquent list and licenses uncollected by him for that month; and also a list of
all persons that have come to his knowledge, or who he believes are not upon his
license list, and charged with the payment of license; and shall pay over to the
Treasurer all licenses collected by him in such month, and report the amount thereof
to the Council, together with the amount delinquent, at the first meeting of ins
Council in each month.

Src. 4. It shall be the duty of the City Clerk to issue a monthly license under
this ordinance to each person so reported to him, and for all other persons known to
the City Clerk; liable to pay a license under this ordinance, duly signed by the
Mayor and Clerk; and to fix and state the amount of license thereon, and on the first
Monday of each month deliver such license to the said Tax Collector for collection,
taking his receipt for the amount thereof; and the said Clerk, in fixing the rate of license
for the several classes in this ordinance hereinbefore specified, shall grade the same
according to his best information and knowledge, and for that purpose may confer
with the persons in interest; and may require any person to file his or her affidavit
as to which class he or she may belong; provided, that in no case shall any mistake
by the Clerk, in fixing the amount of said license, prevent the collection of what
shall be actually due, with all costs against any one selling wlthout license or
refusing to pay such rate so fixed by the Clerk. It shall be the further duty of said
Clerk, immediately after the delinquent list has been delivered to him, to deliver
the licenses uncollected to the Chief of Police, whose duty it shall be to at once
proceed to collect the same, in his discretion, by suit or otherwise. Nothing herein,
however, shall prevent a criminal prosecution, as provided in section 1, for any
violation of the provisions of this ordinance.

Src. 5. In all cases of licenses to keep a bar, saloon, grocery or dance-house,
the person applying for the same shall give a bond with two or more sureties, to be
approved by the mayor, before the delivery of any license, in the sum of two thous-
and dollars, to the City of Los Angeles, conditioned that they will pay all licenses due
to the city under this ordinance or any other ordinance amendatory hereof; and they
will keep a quiet and orderly house, and upon the indication and appearance of any
disturbance or threatened breach of the peace therein, that they will take prompt and
immediate action to secure the arrest of the disorderly person or suppression of any
disorderly conduct on the premises so occupied by them, and that they will not
permit Indians to obtain liquor at their places of business, directly or indirectly, upon
any consideration whatever; nor suffer any drunken Indians to remain about the
saloon and premises under their control.

Src. 6. All ordinances or parts of ordinances conflicting herewith, are hereby
repealed.

and shall cause the same to be published once in English in the Los Angeles Daily

RESOLUTION No. 9.

A Rusoturion of the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, authorizing
the advertising and redemption of certain bonds of the City of Los Angeles.

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, as follows:

Srcrion 1. Whereas, the people of the State of California, represented in
Senate and Assembly, did, by an act approved April 2, 1870, enact a law entitled :
“An Act to Fund the.Debt of the City of Los Angeles, and to provide for the pay-
ment of the same,” which act was to take effect on the first day of July, 1870; and
‘whereas, in pursuance of the provisions of said act, the Common Council of the City
of Los Angeles did cause to be issued bonds of the City of Los Angeles, to the
amount of eighty-seven thousand and fifty dollars, which bonds were made, bearing
- interest at the rate of seven per cent.-per annum from the date of their issue, paya-
ple at the office of the City Treasurer of Los Angeles City, upon the Ist day of May
of each year, and the principal sum thereof payable at said Treasurer's office upon
the Ist day of May, 1895, which bonds were duly signed by the Mayor and Presi-
dent of the Board of Common Council of the City of Los Angeles and the City
Treasurer, and with the seal of said city stamped thereon, and with coupons
attached to said bonds, the first for the interest ending May Ist, 1871, and the
remainder for one year’s interest each year thereafter, and all consecutively num-
bered and attached to said bonds; and whereas, by section 12 of said act, it is pro-
vided that for the payment of the principal and interest of the said bonds, and until
the same are paid and discharged, a tax of twenty-five cents on each one hundred
dollars shall be annually levied on each one hundred dollars’ worth of real and per-
sonal property in said city, and applied to the payment of interest on said bonds,
and the remainder of said fund, after piying the annual interest, to be applied to
the liquidation of the principal of said bonds, and to be known as the interest and
sinking fund of 1870; and whereas, there are now of said issue bonds to the amount
of eighty-five thousand eight hundred dollars, with interest thereon from the Ist
day of May, 1878, unpaid; and whereas, there is now in said interest and sinking
fund the sum of $15,248.28 gold coin of the United States; now, therefore, be it

Resolved, by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, thatthe City
Treasurer of the City of Los Angeles be, and the same is hereby directed, to adver-
tise for two weeks in the Los Angeles Daily EVENING EXPRESS, a newspaper pub-
lished in the City of Los Angeles, for sealed proposals, to be opened at the session
of thé Council of said city next ensuing after the last publication thereof, in open

session thereof, for the surrender of bonds issued under said Act, which advertise-
ment shall state the amount of money he has on hand for the purpose of redemp-
tion, and shall require said proposals to be acecompanied by an undertaking, signed
by the person making the proposal, that the same shall be carried out within fifteen
days after the acceptance of the same, which said undertaking shall be in the penal
sum of one thousand dollars, conditioned that if said proposal is accepted, that the
obligor will, within fifteen days from the time of the acceptance of the same, sur-
render the amount of bonds of said issue named in said proposal.

Src. 2. When said proposals are opened, the Council shall accept the lowest


===== PDF PAGE 19 = PRINTED PAGE 19 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. ' 19

proposals, at rates not exceeding par value, as may redeem the greatest. amount of
bonds, until the cash on hand for redemption is exhausted.

Sec. 3. The surrender of said bonds in pursuance of the provisions of this res- /
olution shall exonerate the City Treasurer from all liability to the City of Los An-
_geles, by reason of the payment made by him for the bonds so surrendered.

Sec. 4. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this resolu-
tion, and shall cause the same to be published once in English in the Los Angeles
Daily Eventve Express, and once in Spanish in La Cronica, and thereupon and

RESOLUTION No. 12.

A REsoLurion providing for the construction of a sewer on Fort street, to be known
as the extension of the Fourth and Fort street branch sewer.

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, as follows:

Section 1. That there be and hereby is ordered to be laid out and constructed,
atthe expense of the property-holders, the real estate of whom is assessable therefor,
a public sewer in said city, to be known and designated as the extension of the
Fourth and Fort street sewer, along and over the following described route, to-wit:
Commencing at a point 120 feet southerly from the southerly line of First street and
at or near the center of Fort street, and running thence with Fort street southerly


===== PDF PAGE 23 = PRINTED PAGE 23 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 23

to an intersection and junction of and with the Fourth and Fort street sewer, at a
point on or about 120 feet southerly from the southerly line of Third street.

~ The sewer shall be laid of “burned clay” or ‘‘ironstone” sewer pipe, in joints of
not less than two feet; to be not less than eight (8) inches in diameter, inside
measurement; joints to be put together with cement mortar, and the whole line to
be laid at least three feet below the surface of the street.

After the sewer is. completed in sections, the earth shall be replaced in trench
around and over pipe and well watered and rammed, and the surface of the street
left in as good condition as before the work had been done.

Where the sewer passes under the street car track, the track shall be preserved
unbroken,.so as to allow of the passage of cars.

During the night lamps shall be kept burning at the ends of each excavation.

* Said excavations shall also be strongly guarded, so as to prevent accidents. .

All work in connection with the sewer shall be done in a good and workmanlike
manner, under the direction of the City Surveyor and the Sewer Committee of the
Council.

Src. 2, The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this resolution,
and shall cause the same to be published once in English in the Los Angeles- Daily
Evenine Express, and once in Spanish in La Cronica, and thereupon and there-
after it shall take effect and be in force.

- the City of Los Angeles, at its session of May 22d, A. D. 1879.

ORDINANCE No. 9.

Aw ORDINANCE to prevent the appropriation of water for irrigation purposes from
Los Angeles River.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

Section 1. All persons are prohibited from in any way interfering with the
free flow of the water of Los Angeles river, or in any way diverting it without per-
mission of the Council of this city.

Src. 2. Any person so interfering with or diverting the flow of said water, or
in, any way obstructing the said river, or the water in any zanja or toma, without
such permission, shall he deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and shall, on conviction,
be imprisoned not exceeding sixty days, or fined not exceeding two hundred dollars,
or both.

. Src. 3. The police of this city are hereby empowered, authorized and directed
to remove all obstructions found in said river or zanjas, and to arrest all persons
found obstructing the same.

Sec 4. .The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordinance,
and cause the same to be published once in English in the Los ‘Angeles Daily
Evenina Express, and once in Spanish in La Cronica, and thereupon and there-
after it shall take effect and be in force.

City of Los Angeles, at its session of June 5th, A. D. 1879.

ORDINANCE No. 10.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

Szérion 1. It shall be unlawful for any person to use the water of Los Angeles
river, the water of said river flowing in any ditch or zanja for irrigation, without a

ORDINANCE No, 14.

An ORDINANCE of the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, relating to the
use of water outside the city limits, for irrigating purposes.

The Mayof and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do- ordain as follows:

Section 1. No person or persons to whom water or permits shall be sold, to
be used for irrigation within the city limits, shall in any manner sell or transfer any
right to use such water for the benefit or advantage of any person or persons outside
of the city limits; nor shall any person or persons irrigate lands belonging to them or
other persons outside of said city limits, with water obtained by such persons by
permit on application made for land inside the city limits; and all persons are
prohibited from using water on lands outside the city limits for irrigating purposes,
granted by the Zanjero or other persons in behalf of the city, for the purpose of
irrigating land inside the city limits.

Src. 2. Any violation of the provisions of this ordinance shall be deemed a
misdemeanor, and shall be punished, on conviction, by a fine not exceeding fifty
dollars, or imprisonment not exceeding thirty days, or both; and it shall be the duty
of the Zanjero to cut off the whole of the supply granted any person violating this
ordinance or any of its provisions immediately, if, while such water is being so used,
it shall come to his knowledge.

Sec. 3. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordinance,
and shall cause the same to be published once in English in the Los Angeles Daily
Morning JourNAL, and once in Spanish in La Cronica, and thereupon and there-
after it shall take effect and be in force.

I certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of | the
City of Los Angeles, at its session of September 11th, A. D. 1879.
W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Approved this 12th day of September, A. D. 1879.

ORDINANCE No. 16.

AN ORDINANCE of the City of Los Angeles relating to delinquent taxes, and amending
an ordinance of said city, approved June 14th, 1872, relating thereto.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

Section 1. An ordinance of the Mayor and Common Council of the City of Los
Angeles, the same being an ordinance providing for the assessment and collection of
taxes, approved June 14, 1872, by Cristobal Aguilar, Mayor, and recorded upon pages
576 to 586 inclusive, of volume VII of the Records of the City of Los Angeles, and
duly published according to law, and also published on pages 105, 106, 107, 108, 109,
110, 111, 112, 113, 114, 115, 116, 117 of the Ordinances and Resolutions of the City of
Los Angeles, compiled and indexed by Wm. M. Caswell, which compilation was
adopted and published by order of the Council of the City of Los Angeles, and are
hereby adopted as the ordinances and resolutions of said city, and now in full force
and éffect, except as they may have been amended since the publication of the said
compilation, is hereby amended as follows: Sections 32, 33, 34, 35, 36 of said
ordinances, recorded in said volume VII of said records of said city, being sections
145, 146, 147, 148 and 149, on pages 111, 112 in said Caswell’s compilation, are
hereby amended by striking out the whole of said sections, and substituting in
place thereof the following, so that said sections shall hereafter read as follows:

Section 32. The municipal taxes for the fiscal year 1879-80, and all taxes levied
subsequent thereto, ‘shall, if not sooner paid, become delinquent on the first Monday
of December of each year, and no such taxes shall be collected or received by the
collector from and after such time, except upon sale of the property therefor according
to law.

Section 33. On the 15th day of December of each year, the City Tax Collector
must deliver to the Ccuncil a true and correct delinquent list of all persons and
property then owing taxes, and at the same time also return the assessment roll.

In the delinquent list so delivered, must be set down in alphabetical or numeri-
cal order, all matters and things contained in the Assessment Book and relating to
delinquent property, :

Section 34. The Council of the City must carefully compare the Delinquent
List with the Assessment Book, and if satisfied that it contains a full and true state-
ment of all taxes due and unpaid, they must foot up the total amount of taxes so
remaining unpaid, credit the City Tax Collector who acted under it, and make a


===== PDF PAGE 33 = PRINTED PAGE 33 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS. ANGELES. 33

final settlement with him of all taxes charged against him on the Assessment Books,
and if said settlement does not correspond with the Treasurer’s receipt, they shall
require an immediate account of any existing deficiency.

Section 35. After settlement with the Tax Collector of the city, as prescribed
in section 34, the Council must add to the Delinquent List five (5) per cent., and on
the 19th day of December, deliver the said list to the City Tax Collector.

Section 36. On the 8th day of January of each year, the City Tax Collector
must publish the Delinquent List in English in the Los Angeles Daily Journan, and
in Spanish in La Cronica, newspapers printed in said city, or in some other
newspaper or newspapers printed in the said city, which must contain the names of
the persons and a description of the property delinquent, the amount of taxes due
opposite each name and description, with the taxes due on personal property when
the estate is liable therefor, or the several taxes are due from the same person. The
City Tax Collector must append and publish with the Delinquent List a notice that
unless the taxes delinquent, together with the costs and percentages, are paid, the
real property, on which such taxes are a lien, will be sold at public auction.

The publication shall be made once a week for three weeks successively, and
state the time and place of sale. The time of sale must not be less than twenty-one
(21) days nor more than twenty-eight (28) days from the first publication, and the
place of sale must be in front of the Tax Collector’s office.

Sec. 2. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordinance,
and cause the same to be published once in English in the Los Angeles Daily
Mornine JOURNAL, and once in Spanish in La Cronica, and thereupon and there-
after it shall take effect and be in force.

I certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of the
City of Los Angeles, at its session of October 23d, 1879.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Approved this 27th day of October, A. D. 1879.
J. R. TOBERMAN,

Mayor.

ORDINANCE No. 17.

Aw Orpinance of the City of Los Angeles, creating the office of Assistant Tax
Collector.

 

 

 

 

 

 


===== PDF PAGE 36 = PRINTED PAGE 36 =====
36 - ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

The Mayor and Council of the City’of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

Section 1. That the office of Assistant Tax Collector is hereby required for
the more efficient government of said city, and the office of Assistant Tax Collector,

to be so called and designated, is hereby created.

Sxc, 2.. The Council of the City of Los Angeles shall, at its third regular meet-
ing in December of each year, or at suc other time as the Council of said city shall
deem necessary, appoint an Assistant Tax Collector, who shall take the oath of office
in like manner as other-city officers, receive his certificate of appointment, and give
bond for the faithful performance of the duties of his office in such sum as the Coun-

cil shall prescribe.

.Sxc. 3. It shall be the duty of such Assistant Tax Collector, in the event of
death, absence from the City of the Tax Collector, or in the event of any vacancy
in the office of Tax Collector, to perform all the duties required by law of the City
Tax Collector, and all duties which may now or may hereafter be prescribed for said
City Tax Collector, by any ordinance, resolution, motion, by-law or regulation of the
Council of the city; and in his absence as aforesaid, to receive and collect all taxes,
licenses and revenues of the city, and pay the same over to the Treasurer of the city
as directed by ordinance, to keep a book which shall contain a record of every deed
given by or on behalf of the city, for real estate sold for delinquent taxes or assess-
ments, which book shall be properly indexed, and shall be at all suitable times
subject to public inspection and reference.

Src. 4. It shall be the duty of the City Tax Collector and said Assistant Tax
Collector to settle with the Treasurer for all moneys collected for the city for taxes
and licenses, to pay the same to the Treasurer on the day of collection, if practica-
ble, and if not practicable, on the succeeding day, and shall, on Thursday of each
week, file with the Council of said city, a report, accompanied with the Treasurer’s
receipt, of all moneys so paid previous to the day of the filing of said report.

Src. 5. A failure to pay over to said Treasurer, as heretofore provided, shall
be deemed a breach of the bond of the party so failing to pay over; provided, how-
ever, the bond of the City Tax Collector shall always be liable for such failure to
pay over, unless in case of death or absence from the city, the Assistant Tax Collec-
tor shall have been at the time of such failure to pay over, in the actual performance
of the duties of the office, under the provisions of this ordinance, and in such actual
performance, responsible for such collection and failure to pay over.

Src. 6. Nothing herein contained shall be construed to deprive the City Tax
Collector of the right to perform any of the duties of his office provided by law, but
only to provide for the proper administration of the duties of the office of Tax
Collector, in case of a vacancy of the same caused by his death, resignation or
otherwise, or during absence from said city of such Tax Collector without permission
of the Council.

Szc. 7. Said Assistant Tax Collector shall receive such salary, either per diem
or otherwise, as the Council of said city shall direct, and shall hold the office merely
at the pleasure of the Council.

Src. 8. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordidaties!

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of the
City of Los Angeles, at its session of December 11th, A. D. 1879.

ORDINANCE No. 18.

AN ORDINANCE of the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, providing for
the prevention of bribery and prostitution, and the protection of the public
streets and flumes.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. Every person who gives or offers any bribe to any police officer or
to any of the police force of the City of Los Angeles, with intent to influence him in
respect to any act or duty imposed upon him by the laws of the State, ordinances,
regulations or orders of the authorities of the City of Los Angeles, the Mayor and
Council, Police Commissioners, or the rules and regulations of the Police Force,
shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and on conviction, shall be punished by fine
not less than twenty dollars, nor exceeding five hundred dollars, or imprisonment
not less than twenty days or exceeding six months, or both.

Sec. 2. It shall be unlawful for any woman, within the limits described in an
ordinance entitled, ‘‘An ordinance to amend an ordinance to prohibit houses of
ill-fame and prostitution in certain parts of the City of Los Angeles,” approved May
25th, 1874, approved March 10th, 1877, approved July 9th 1878, to offer her bedy
for purposes of prostitution, or solicit any man for money or purposes of prostitution;
to have carnal intercourse, or to commit fornication.

Any person violating this section shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and
shall, on conviction, be punished by fine not exceeding one hundred dollars, or by
imprisonment not exceeding sixty days, or both.


===== PDF PAGE 39 = PRINTED PAGE 39 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 39

Sec. 3. ‘It shall be unlawful for any person to herd any horse, sheep, goats,
swine or neat cattle or other animals on any street or highway in this city, or allow
the same to graze on any street in this city.

Any person violating this section shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and
shall, on conviction, be punished by a fine not exceeding ten dollars, or imprisonment
not exceeding ten days.

Src. 4. It shall be unlawful for any person to hitch or tie any horse, cow or
other animal to any flume constructed for the purpose of carrying water for irrigating
purposes. ) :

Any violation of this section shall be deemed a misdemeanor, and punishable,
on conviction, by fine not exceeding ten dollars, or by imprisonment not exceeding
ten days, or both. ’

Suc. 5. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordinance,
and cause the same to be published once in English in the Los Angeles Daily
Mornine JouRNAL, and thereupon it shall take effect and be in force.

T hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles, at its session of January 31st, 1880.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Approved this 2d day of February, A. D. 1880.

The said sewer shall be constructed in accordance with the followmg specifica-
dons: .

The sewer is to be either cement or burned clay glazed pipe, or ai brick. or a
wooded pipe coated with asphaltum. with the necessary branches or comneciions at
every sixty feet on each side, to accommodate the property on the lme of the sewer,
and Y branches opposite all streets crossing the alignment of the sewer, and with

man-holes at every 1000 feet.

The earth along the route shall be excavated to the peice shown on the profile
in the City Surveyor’s office. and to the proper shape to receive the sewer.

Pre SEWER.

Tf pipes are used, they will be from Macy street to Aliso street of 12-inch
diameter in the clear, from Aliso io First street of 14-inch, and from Firsé street 70
Ogier Lane of 16 inches diameter. They are to be carefully laid with fall joints of
mortar, composed of equal parts of white Portland cement and clear sharp sand.

Tn making and fitting the joints, care must be taken to pomt and make smooth
the mortar on the inside of each joint, before the mortar sets.

The Y branches or connections for the accommodation of the property aligning
the sewer, shall not be less than six inches in diameter.

The Y branches or connections for the cross-streets shall be eight inches diameter,

 

 

 

 


===== PDF PAGE 47 = PRINTED PAGE 47 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 47

and present an angle of forty-five degrees with and in the direction of the flow of the
current.

The exterior ends of the branches are to be securely closed by caps of the same
material as the pipes, when not immediately used. :

The connections with the main sewer must be carefully made without injury to
the pipe of either sewer.

The man-hole will be of the same pipe as the sewer, connected by a T joint, and
carried up to within six inches of the surface of the ground, and provided with a
two-inch thick rough redwood cover, well nailed and cleated.

The earth filled in over and around the pipe must be free of stones: and other
hard substances for at least one foot next to the pipe; the pipe to be hard burned
glazed, also the connections.

Brick WoRK.

If the sewer be made of brick it will be made of circular cross-section, with an
inside diameter of 20 inches, and walls of 4 or 8 inches in thickness. The brick to
be used are to be first-class, sound, hard-burned. The bidders to deposit a specimen
brick in the office of the City Surveyor.

The brick work of the invert shall be bedded on sand.

The joints are to be well filled, and not greater mortar joints than one inch, unless
otherwise directed. !

All inside joints to be well jointed; the bricks to be laid in such positions as the
Committee of the Council on Sewers and the City Surveyor shall direct during the
progress of the work.

Man-holes shall be constructed at distances of 1000/feet apart, or such other
distances as may be directed; but the whole number shall average one to each 1000
feet of sewer. :

For a man-hole, a brick wall, of eight or four inches in thickness, shall be
carried up from the sewer to within six inches of the surface of the ground, forming
a cylinder of twenty inches inside diameter.

_ Man-hole covers to be furnished of 2-inch thick rough redwood, well nailed and
cleated.

The sewer is to be cement pipe, to be composed of one part imported White's
Portland cement, one part native lime, three and a half parts sand, two parts
medium gravel; to be well rammed in strong moulds, and to be of the thickness of
1g inches, with the necessary branches or connections at every sixty feet on each

all streets crossing the alignment of the sewer, and with man-holes at every 1000
feet.

~ The earth along the Toute shall be excavated to the grade, shown on the profile
in the City Surveyor’s office, and be the proper shape to receive the sewer.

Pirz SEWER.

The pipe used will be from point of commencement at south line of Macy street
to center of Aliso street, 12 inches in diameter in the clear; thence to points on
Alameda street 291 feet northerly from the north line of First street, 14 inches in
diameter in the clear;

Thence by the previously-described route to connect with the main sewer at
Ogier Lane of 16 inches diameter in the clear.

They are to be carefully laid with full joints of mortar, composed of equal parts
of White’s Portland ‘cement and clear sharp sand.

In making and fitting the joints, care must be taken to point and make smooth
the mortar on the inside of each joint, before the mortar sets.

The Y branches or connections for the accommodation of the property aligning
the sewer, shall not be less than six inches in diameter.

The Y branches or connections for the cross-streets shall be eight inchesin diameter,
and present an angle of forty-five degrees with and in the direction of the flow of the
current. i

The exterior ends of the branches are to be securely closed by caps of the same
material as the pipes, when not immediately used.

The connections with the main sewer must be carefully made without injury to
the pipe of either sewer.

The man-hole will be of the same pipe as the sewer, connected by a T joint, and
carried up to within six inches of the surface of the ground, and provided\with a
two-inch thick rough redwood cover, well nailed and cleated.

The earth filled in over and around the pipe must be free of stones and other
hard substances for at least one foot next to the pipe.

The earth taken from the excavations is to be refilled over the sewer and around
the pipes, well watered and rammed, and on completion of tle work, the surplus
material, if any, to be removed, and the streets or surface of the ground put in as
good condition as it was at the commencement of the work; when the sewer passes

ORDINANCE No. 20.

AN Orpryance of the City of Los Angeles, relating to the regulation, sale and
disposition of the water and zanjas of the city for irrigating purposes.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

Section 1. The following is the price of water for irrigating inside the city

limits, to-wit:
For one day, two (2) dollars per head.
For one-half day, one dollar and twenty-five ($1.25) cents per head.
For one night, one dollar and twenty-five ($1.25) cents per head.
For one hour, fifty (50) cents per head.
One day shall be regarded from sunrise to sunset.

Sec. 2. The Zanjero shall reserve one head of water on every zanja between
the hours of 12 M. and sunset of Thursday of each week, in order to supply persons
desiring water by the hour.

Sec. 3. All persons desiring hour water on any zanja shall apply for the same
at least three days prior to the Thursday for which the application is made, and the
Zanjero shall, on said Thursday, distribute the water to the applicants therefor im
the order of their applications; if any of said water remains unsold on said Thursday,
the Zanjero shall sell the same in the order for which it is applied at the same rate;
provided, however, that the Zanjero shall not grant more than one hour’s water on
any zanja, to any person, if, by so doing, others who have applied within the time
specified shall be deprived thereof.

Sec. 4. If at any time there shall be a surplus of water unsold at the times
specified in the ordinances of said city’ providing for the time of applying for water
for irrigating purposes, the Zanjero may grant the use of the several zanjas of said

ORDINANCE No, 23.

AN ORDINANCE to prevent fast riding and driving upon all bridges of twenty foot.
span in the City of Los Angeles, and protect them from being injured or defaced. _

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

‘Sgcrron 1. It shall be unlawful for any horseman, or the driver of any wagon,
carriage or buggy or other vehicle, or of any kind of stock or cattle, to ride, lead or ,
drive upon, over or across any public bridge extending over Los Angeles river in this
city, or any other bridge maintained by the authorities of said city, exceeding
twenty feet span, extending over any zanja, wroyo, creek, stream, baranca, gulch |
or excavation within the City of Los Angeles, at any rate of speed faster than a —
walk.

Sec. 2. It shall further be unlawful for any person to injure or deface the
same or any part thereof, by cutting or by posting thereon of any hand-bill, circular,
advertisement or other notice whatever, painted, printed or written.

Sec. 3. Amy person violating any of the provisions of this ordinance shall,
upon conviction thereof before any competent court, be fined for the first offense in
a sum not less than five dollars, nor exceeding twenty dollars and costs; and upon
conviction for any subsequent offense, under this ordinance, such person shall be
fined in a sum not less than ten dollars nor more than fifty dollars and costs, one-
half of which fines, exclusive of costs, shall be paid to the informer who may have

procured the conviction.

Sec. 4. This ordinance shall take effect and be in force from and after its
passage, approval and publication, and all ordinances and parts of ordinances in
conflict with this ordinance shall be and the same are hereby repealed.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles, at its session of July 10th, 1880.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Approved the 14th day of July, A. D. 1880.

ORDINANCE No. 27. —

AN ORDINANCE to provide for the licensing of solicitors and runners, and for the
protection of passengers.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. All hotels, boarding-houses, inns, lodging-houses, or places where

board and lodging is furnished per day, shall, for any runner, solicitor, or agent,

directly or indirectly employed to solicit or obtain guests, boarders, or lodgers, pay
for each agent, solicitor or runner, a license to said city of $1 per month.

Sec. 2. Each runner, agent or solicitor shall, while engaged in the business of
soliciting custom for the hotel or place he represents, wear a badge, which badge
shall be numbered, and the number recorded with the Chief of Police, with the name
of the person having the right to wear said number, and all other persons are forbid-
den to use cr wear such number without first changing the name attached thereto,
recorded with the said Chief of Police.

Sec. 3. All persons not the’ owners or solicitors of hotels, boarding-houses,
lodging-houses, or places where boarding and lodging may be obtained for pay, own-
ing or driving any hack, cab or other vehicle for the conveyance of passengers, may
-also solicit passengers to be carried in their said conveyance, or their baggage; but
said persons must also have a number, with the name of the person using said num-
ber, recorded with the Chief of Police as aforesaid. ;

Sec. 4. The Chief of Police of said city, shall, at every railway station in said
city where trains of cars carrying passengers shall stop, arrange a place where all
solicitors, agents, runners and other persons having the legal right to solicit
passengers for the purposes aforesaid, or any other purpose, shall, at the time of the
arrival of the train at said station, stand; and it shall be unlawful for such persons
to leave ‘the place so designated for the ‘purpose of soliciting or requesting any
passengers-or other persons; and any such runners, solicitors, agents or other
persons who shall leave the place so designated for the purpose of soliciting custom,
either for himself or others, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor..

All persons, except those herein enumerated, and who may be licensed by said
city, are prohibited from soliciting or requesting any passenger to ‘carry him or her
by any conveyance or otherwise, or their baggage, within the limits of the city.

All violations of this ordinance shall be punished by a fine not exceeding $50,
nor less than $10, or imprisonment not exceeding thirty days, or both.

Src. 5. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordinance,
and cause the same to be published once in English in the Daily Evrenine
EXPRESS, a newspaper published in said city, and oon and thereafter it shall
take effect and be in force.

_  Ihereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of the —
City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of November 27th, A. D. 1880.
W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.
Approved this 29th day of November, A.D. 1880.
J. R. TOBERMAN,
/ Mayor.

ORDINANCE No. 32.

‘Aw OnpINANce relative to the execution of deeds of conveyance to parties petition-
ing for the same, and repealing an ordinance relating thereto entitled ‘‘An ordi-
nance relative to the execution of deeds of conveyance to parties petitioning for
the same,” approved January 10th, 1873.


===== PDF PAGE 78 = PRINTED PAGE 78 =====
78 “ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Srcrion 1. That hereafter all parties applying for the execution of any deed or
deeds of conveyance from the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, for the
purpose and with the object of covering defects in their title already claimed by
them, shall present to the Mayor and Council a petition in writing, and verified
before some officer authorized to administer oaths, setting forth in detail all the
facts upon which they may claim to be entitled to such conveyance or conveyances;
and'shall, at the same time, and accompanying the same petition, submit to the said
Mayor and Council a full and complete abstract of title to and a map or plot
of the land described in said petition, and to be affected by such deed or deeds of

conveyance.

Suc. 2. No deed or other evidence of title solicited for the purpose aforesaid,
shall be executed or delivered to any party or parties for any land within said city of
Los Angeles unless said party or parties applying therefor shall, before or at the
time of such delivery, pay to the Mayor of said city, the whole amount of all the
taxes and assessments which either have been laid and imposed upon said property
and remain delinquent and unpaid, or which may or should have been assessed
against it during the time such party or parties, or his or their grantor or grantors,
have had or claimed to have had the possession of or title to the property described
in the petition. Nor shall any deed or other evidencejof title be executed or deliv-
ered by the Mayor of said city to any party or parties, unless the same shall first
have been ordered by the Council.

Src. 3. If it shall appear from any investigation of the title that the parties
applying for such deed are equitably entitled thereto, and are in the exclusive and
undisturbed possession of said land, and that there is no valid or legal objection
thereto, a deed may, upon the recommendation of the Council, issue to the applicant
for such land, which deed will convey all the right, title and interest of the city
therein to the grantee in the deed.

Src. 4. An ordinance entitled ‘‘An ordinance relative to the execution of deeds
of conveyance to parties petitioning for the same,” approved January 10, 1873, is
hereby repealed, and so are all ordinances or resolutions in conflict herewith re-
pealed.

Szc. 5. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage. of this ordi-
nance, and shall cause the same to be published in English once in the Daily EVENING
Express, and thereupon it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of the
City of Los Angeles, at its regular meeting of February 5th, 1881.
W. W. ROBINSON,
- Clerk of the Council ‘of the City of Los Angeles.

ORDINANCE No. 33,” ,

AN ORDINANCE providing for licensing the sale-of opium in the City of Los An-
geles.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

‘Secrron 1. Tt shall’be unlawful for any person or persons t) sell, barter or ex-
change any opium in the City of Los Angeles, except for scientific or medicinal pur-
poses, or on the prescription of a “practicing physician, without first procuring a
license therefor, in accordance herewith. - Such license shall be known and desig-
nated as an opium dealer’s license, and ‘any violation of ‘this ordinance jshall be
deemed a misdemeanor, and any person violating any of the provisions hereof shall
be guilty ofa misdemeanor, and -shall be punished by a fine not exceeding
$300, or by impristnment not exceeding six months in the county jail, or by both
such fine and imprisonment.

Sec. 2. Hach person and firm that shall be engaged in the practice of selling or
exchanging any opium, whether on commission or otherwise, as a broker for the
owner or consignee, shall pay a license therefor as follows:

First Class.—Those doing business in the aggregate amount of five hundred

- dollars per quarter, shall constitute first-class opium dealers, and must. pay a license
therefor of twenty dollars per month.

Second Class.—Those doing business in the aggregate amount of three hundred
dollars per quarter, or less, shall constitute second-class, and pay a license of fifteen
dollars per month. ;

Sec. 3. All ordinances and resolutions so far as conflicting herewith, are hereby
repealed.

Sze. 4. All prosecutions tnder this ordinance must be had’: porore the City —
Justice of this city.

~ ORDINANCE No. 34.
An Orprnance to establish regulations of water rates, furnished to the inhabitants —
of the City of Los Angeles, for the year commencing on July 1st, 1881.

“The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

Sxction 1, The rates to be charged for water by any corporation, company or
individual now furnishing water'to the inhabitants of the City of Los Angeles, or to/
furnish the same hereafter, shall be and are as follows, for the.year commencing
July Ist, 1881, and the following schedule of rates is hereby established and declared
to be the water rates for said city during said period:

SCHEDULE oF WATER’ RATES.

For tenements occupied by a single family of not more than five persons, $2; j
for each additional person, 25c.

Bathing tubs in private houses, for each tub, 50c. \

In public houses, boarding houses, bathing establishments, barber ae on each
tub, $3.

Bakeries, according to the monthly use of flour, for each 25 barrels, $2.

Boarding schools, in addition to the rate of private families, for each scholar, 15c.

Building purposes, by contract only, for each barrel of lime, 2oc.

Fountains, by contract only.

Private houses, including water for washing carriages, for one horse, 25¢.

Omnibuses, stage stables, for each horse, 50c.

Truckmen’s, cart and saddle horses, 374c. a

Provided that in no case shall any stable be charged less than $2. a

For each horse-trough on sidewalk, $2 to $5. - - 2

All street sprinkling free,

Hotels, taverns and boarding houses, not including water for baths, for use

 

 


===== PDF PAGE 87 = PRINTED PAGE 87 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 87

without the house, for each bed for boarders or lodgers within the same, in addition
to the rate for private families, 25c.

For each day boarder, 20c.

Lodging houses, in addition to rate of family keeping the house for accommoda-
tion, for each person within the same, 20c.

Sprinkling gardens and grounds during the summer months, for each lot of not
more than 50 feet front, -50c; for each additional 50 feet front, or part thereof, 50c.

Porter houses, groceries, refectories &c., shall be charged from $2 to $10.

Printing offices by agreement.

Railroad corporations, rate subject to agreement in accordance with the quan-
tity of water used. _

Steam engines, according to quantity of water used, by agreement or by meter.

Stores, offices, warehouses and tenements, not included in any other classifica-
tion, and requiring only an ordinary amount of water, not less than $2,

For each public water-closet, $2; for each private water-closet, 75c.

For large quintities of water, where the quantity used does not exceed 15,000
gallons per month, there shall be charged for each 1,000 gallons consumed, as ascer-
tained by meter or otherwise, $1.25; where the quantity is over 15,000 gallons per
month, for each 1,000 gallons, $1.

The party furnishing water shall- have the power in all cases to ascertain by
meter or otherwise, the quantity of water used by any consumer, and charge in
accordance with the quantity so ascertained, instead of the special rate given
above. d

For water required for purposes which are not specified in the foregoing tariff,
. the rate shall be fixed by agreement between the parties.

The party furnishing water will insert the tap and introduce the service-pipe to
the curb-stone by their authorized tapper for twelve dollars, the pipes and fillings
remaining the property of the party furnishing the same.

All water rates payable monthly, in advance.

Payments will not be received for a less period than one month.

Applicants for water at any time after the first of any month, shall pay their
rates to the end of the following month.

That all of said rates are payable in gold or silver coin.

Src. 2. All parts of ordinances in conflict herewith are hereby repealed.

Sec. 38. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordinance,
and shall cause the same to be published in English once in the Los Angeles Daily
Eventne Express, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in
force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of the
City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of the 24th day of February, A. D. 1881.

ORDINANCE No. 30.

Aw ORDINANCE of the Council of the City of Los Angeles, providing for the mode
and manner of assessing and collecting the expense of constructing and improv-
Ing sewers or drains in Los Angeles city.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain ‘as follows:

SectioN 1. The mode and manner of apportioning the estimated cost of
improvements of streets prescribed in section 18, article IX of the Revised Charter
for the City of Los Angeles, approved March 30, 1878, shall apply to the construc-
tion of such sewers or drains ordered to be constructed, improved or made in said
city.

And when the Council of said city shall not direct the mode and manner of
apportioning the estimated cost of such construction or improvement, nor otherwise
direct how the same shall be assessed or paid, then such expenses shall in every
respect be assessed and collected in the same manner as is provided in case of street
improvements; provided that no credit mentioned in section 18 shall be made in any
assessment for construction of sewers, excepting where the property owner has
already paid for and connected with another sewer or sewers, or where a party can-
not beneficially connect the sewage of such property with such sewer, such property
shall be exempted from such assessment. : \ \

Src. 2. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordinance,
and shall cause the same to be published once in English in the Los Angeles Daily
Eventne Express, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in
force. :

T hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Couzey of the
City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of oe 9th, A. D. 1881.

. W. ROBINSON, :
Clerk of the a fi the City of Los Angeles.

Approved this 12th day of April, A. D. 1881.
J. R. TOBERMAN,

Mayor.

indebtedness be refunded under the provisions of sections 4445-6-7-8-9, of the Polit-
ieal Code of the State of California; therefore, be it resolved, that there shall be
issued one hundred and twenty-six (126) bonds of said city in the amount of sixty-
three thousand ($63,000) dollars, in denominations of $500 each, bearing date’ J uly
Ist, 1881, and shall be payable at the office of the City Treasurer of said city, on the
Ist day of July, A. D. 1901, or at any time before that day, at the pleasure of said
eity, which shall draw interest at the rate of 7 per cent. per annum, payable semi-
annually on the first day of July and January of each year.

The President of the Council of said city is hereby authorized to sign said
bonds, and the City Auditor shall attest the same.

The coupons attached to said bonds shall be signed by the City Auditor.

executed, consecutively numbered and sealed, they shall be delivered to the Treas-
urer of said city, and the said Treasurer is hereby authorized and directed to
exchange said bonds (but im no case for a less sum than the face value of said bonds,

the City of Los Angeles, and authorizing the Common Council of that city to issue

bonds for a special school-building fund,’ approved February 24, 1872.

Treasurer is hereby authorized to allow and\compute interest on all bonds surren-

appearance of any disturbance or threatened breach of the peace therein, that they

will take prompt and immediate action to secure the arrest of the disorderly person,

that they will not permit Indians to obtain liquor at their places of business,
directly or indirectly, upon any consideration whatever; nor suffer any drunken
Indians to remain about the saloon and premises under their control.

ORDINANCE No. 38.

Aw Orp1naNncE in relation to fast driving in the City of Los Angeles.
The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

Section 1. It shall be unlawful for any hackman, coach driver, carriage driver,
or driver of any milk wagon, wagon, carriage rockaway, buggy, truck, dray, cart,
delivery, job or express wagon, or of any two or four-wheeled vehicle whatever, or
driver of any animal or team attached to any such vehicle or any vehicle whatever,
to drive at an immoderate gait or dangerous rate of speed, within the streets, parks
or public grounds of the City of Los Angeles; and it shall also be unlawful for any

_ such driver to permit the horse, animal or team attached to any such vehicle to
gallop, run or race within such streets, parks or other public grounds of said city, or
to travel at an immoderate gait or dangerous rate of speed; and it shall also be
unlawful for any person under the age of eighteen years to drive or be permitted to
drive any omnibus, coach or hack; and each hackman shall wear in a conspicuous
place upon his person a badge designating the number of his hack.


===== PDF PAGE 106 = PRINTED PAGE 106 =====
106 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

 

Sec. 2. Any person violating any of the provisions of this ordinance shall be

deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and, wpon conviction thereof by any court having
jurisdiction thereof, shall be fined therefor in a sum not less than five dollars, nor more

than three hundred dollars, or shall be imprisoned for a term not exceeding ninety
days, or both.

Sec, 3. All ordinances and parts of ordinances, in so far as they conflict with
this ordinance, and no further, shall be and the same are hereby repealed.

Sec. 4. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordinance,
and shall cause the same to be published once in English in the Los Angeles Daily

Evrentne Express, and thereupon and thereafter it'shall take effect and be in
force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of June 11th, A. D. 1881.

ORDINANCE: No. 42.

An OrpinancE forbidding all persons without a permit, to open or dig up any of
the streets in the City of Los Angeles.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. It shall be unlawful for any person or persons to open, dig up,
excavate or in any manner injure by digging or excavating, any of the public streets
in the City of Los Angeles, without a written permit, signed by the Clerk of said —

Council, so to do.

Src. 2. The Clerk of said Council shall issue no permit for sewer connections
without an order of the Council or the Committee on Sewers to that effect.

Src. 38. The provisions hereof shall apply to all persons or corporations,
. whether acting under a charter or right heretofore grinted or not; and no excavation ~
shall hereafter be made in any of the streets of said city for the purpose of laying
down any pipe to conduct water, gas, sewerage or any other substance, nor shall
any pipe be laid down at all or any excavation whatever, made without permission

herein provided for first having been obtained.

Src. 4. All persons violating any of the provisions of this ordinance shall be
guilty of a misdemeanor, and shall be fined in a sum not less than ten dollars, and

not more than three hundred dollars.

Sxc. 5. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordinance,
and shall cause the same to be published once in English in the Los Angeles Daily
Evenine Express, and thereupon it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of July 16th, A. D. 1881.

W. W. ROBINSON,
-Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Approved this 18th day of July, A. D. 1881.
J. R. TOBERMAN,

Mayor.
Published July 18th, A. D. 1881. ;

ORDINANCE No. 43.

Aw OrpINANCE prohibiting all persons, except employees, from getting on and off
railroad cars while said cars are in motion.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows: _

Section 1. It shall be unlawful for any person to get upon or attempt to get
upon any car or train of cars propelled by steam, or such as are usually propelled by
steam, within the corporate limits of the City of Los Angeles while such car or tram
is in motion.

 


===== PDF PAGE 117 = PRINTED PAGE 117 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. LY

*

Sgc. 2. It shall be unlawful for any person, at any place within the limits of

- said city, to get upon any car or train of cars propelled by steam, with intent to

jump from or leave such car or train while the same is in motion; provided, the

provisions of this ordinance shall not apply to the owners of or persans engaged in
operating such car or train.

Sec, 3. Any person violating any of the provisions of this ordinance shall,
upon conviction thereof, be fined in any sum not exceeding fifty dollars, or by
imprisonment in the county jail not exceeding twenty-five days, or by both such
fine and imprisonment.

Src. 4. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordinance,
and shall cause the same to be published once in English in the Eventna Express,
a daily newspaper published in the City of Los Angeles, and thereupon and there-
after it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of the
City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of the 4th day of June, A. D. 1881.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

The above ordinance was presented to the Mayor for his approval June 7th, A.
D. 1881, and has not been returned by him to the Clerk of the Council at this date,
viz: July 2lst, A. D. 1881. By reason of not being returned within fifteen days
(Sundays and other legal holidays excepted), the above ordinance has become
effective, and as valid as if the Mayor had approved and signed it.
W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Published July 2lst, A. D. 1881.

RESOLUTION No. 75.

A Resonutron of the City of Los Angeles, providing for the improvement and
grading of Fifth street, between Olive and Charity streets. 4

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, as follows:

Section 1. That the following improvements, at the expense of the property
owners, shall be made on Fifth street, between Olive and Charity streets.

Sec. 2. The street shall be graded in the following manner:

The road-bed shall be graded and covered with eight inches of gravel. The
crown of the street shall be four inches above the grade of the north curb of the street,
with such a slope toward the curb that at the outside of the gutter it shall be ten
inches below the grade. After being graveled, it shall be thoroughly wet and then
rolled, provided that there shall be no stones in said gravel larger than two inches

in diameter. :
The gutters shall be 34 feet wide and paved with granite cobble stones not less

than eight inches long, thoroughly set in sand and then rammed. —The center of
the gutter shall be fourteen inches, and the outside adjoining the road-bed ten inches |

below the grade.
The curb shall be of redwood, 3x12 inches, placed with the top to the estab-

lished grade, spiked to posts of redwood, 4x4 inches three feet long, set into the
ground full length below the top of the curb and inside of the same, and not
more than four feet apart, with one to each joint in the curbing.

The sidewalks shall be nine feet wide, graded and covered with three inches
of fine gravel, smoothly laid, and raked free from coarse stones of more than one
inch in diameter. The slope to the sidewalks shall be three inches toward the curb.

Sec. 3. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this resolution,
and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily HERALD,
a newspaper published in said city, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take

effect and be in force.
I hereby certify that the foregoing resolution was adopted by the Council of the
City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of September 10th, A. D. 1881.

Aldermen or other legislative body of any city and county, city or town fo
obtain data and information from any corporation, company or person supplying
water to such city and county, city or town, requiring such Boards, Town
Council or other legislative body to perform the duties prescribed by section
one, of article fourteen, of the Constitution, and prescribing penalties for the
non-performance of such duties.” e

The Mayor and Council of tHe City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

Section 1. All corporations, companies or persons furnishing water to the
inhabitants of the City of Los Angeles for domestic purposes, are hereby required,
ordered and directed, pursuant to the provisions of the act in the title hereof
referred to, to furnish the Council of the City of Los Angeles, during the month of
January of each and every year, a detailed statement, verified by the oath of the
President and Secretary of such corporation, company or individual, which state-
ment must show the name of each water-rate payer, his or her place of residence, and
the amount paid for water during the year preceding the date of such statement,
and which statement shall and must also show all revenue derived from all sources,
and an itemized statement of expenditures made for supplying water during said
time.

Src. 2. Said company, corporation or individual is also hereby ordered,
directed and required, as required by section 3 of said act of the Legislature, to
present with the first statement filed, as provided in section one of this ordinance, a
detailed statement verified in like manner as*the statement mentioned in section one
hereof, showing the amount of money actually expended annually since commencing
business, in the purchase, construction and maintenance respectively of the property
necessary to the carrying on of its business, and also the gross cash receipts annually
for the same period from all sources.

Src. 3. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordinance,
and shall cause the same to be published once in English in the Daily Los Angeles
HERALD, a newspaper published in said city, and thereupon and thereafter it shall
take effect and be in force.
