ORDINANCE No. 48.

AN ORDINANCE of the Mayor and Council of Los Angeles city for the protection of
life and property by fire, and regulations concerning the erection of buildings.

The Mayor and Council of Los Angeles city do ordain as follows:

Section 1. Thatall that portion of the City of Los Angeles bounded and described
as follows, to-wit: Commencing at the point in the intersection of Ninth and Pearl
streets, and running thence northerly along the middle line of Pearl street to Canal
and Reservoir street, thence along the middle line of Canal and Reservoir street

“south-easterly to Castellar street, thence northerly along the middle line of Castellar
street extended to the river Los Angeles, thence down the river Los Angeles
southerly to Seventh street, thence westerly along the middle line of Seventh street
to San Pedro street, thence along the middle line of San Pedro street southerly to
Moran lane, thence along the middle line of Moran lane north-westerly to Main
street, thence westerly along the middle line of Ninth street to the place of
beginning, shall be the general Fire Limits of the City of Los Angeles.


===== PDF PAGE 136 = PRINTED PAGE 136 =====
 

TB 6c4s ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

Sec. 2. That the general Fire Limits of the City of Los Angeles, as hereinbefore
established, shall be and the same are hereby divided into two districts, to be

known and designated respectively as District No. 1 of the general Fire Limits of

the City of Los Angeles, and as District No. 2 of the general Fire Limits of the
City of Los Angeles.

Src. 3. The boundaries of the respective districts shall be as follows:

First.—District No. 1 of the general Fire Limits of the City of Los Angeles
shall comprise and embrace all that portion of the general Fire Limits bounded and
described as follows, to-wit:

Commencing at the intersection of the middle line of Alameda and Marchessault
streets and running thence southerly along the middle line of Alameda street to
Requena street, thence along the middle line of Requena street westerly to Wil-
mington street, thence along the middle line of Wilmington street southerly to
First street, thence along the middle line of First street westerly to Fort street,
thence along the middle line of Fort street northerly to Temple street, thence along
the middle line of Temple street easterly to New High street, thence along the
middle line of New High street to Marchessault street, thence along the middle line
of Marchessault street easterly to the place of beginning.

Second.—District No. 2 of the general Fire Limits of the City of Los Angeles
shall comprise and embrace all that portion of the general Fire Limits of the City of
Los Angeles not included within the boundaries of District No. 1 as above provided.

Sec. 4. It shall be and is unlawful for any person, persons, firm or corporation
to store, permit the storage of or keep for sale within the general Flre Limits of the
City of Los Angeles in any one building: .

First.--Any quantity of hay of any kind exceeding three tons in weight.

Second.—Any petroleum, gasoline or any product of petroleum or hydro-carbon
liquids, unless the same are kept in iron tanks, and in no larger quantities than one

hundred and fifty gallons.
Third.—Any Hercules, dyamite, giant powder or any kind of blasting powder

or gun-powder in any quantity over fifty pounds.

Sze. 5. It shall be and is unlawful for any person or persons, firm or corpora-
tion to store, permit the storage of or keep for sale within the general Fire Limits of
the City of Los Angeles, any refined petroleum in larger quantities than two hundred
gallons, the same to be always kept in metal cans, and the said oil shall stand a fire

test of 110 degrees Fahrenheit.

. xc. 6. It shall be and is unlawful for any person, persons, firm or corporation
to manufacture within the general Fire Limits of the City of Los Angeles any acids
or any other combustible or explosive chemicals, to boil or refine oils or to manutfac-

ture matches.

Sec. 7. No person shall use any portable light in any building or place where
combustible materials or hay is kept, unless such light be securely enclosed in a
lantern.

 

Sec. 8. Each person making, using or having charge or control of shavings, : s

 


===== PDF PAGE 137 = PRINTED PAGE 137 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 37.

hay, straw, sacks, bags, litter or any other combustible waste or fragments, which
are generally accumulated in the yards of stores, same shall be removed once in _
every two weeks.

Sec. 9. All warehouses used for storage of any kind of powder, gasoline, crude
petroleum, or any product of petroleum which shall flash or emit ian inflammable
vapor at a temperature below 110° Fahrenheit, must be located outside the general
Fire Limits of the City of Los Angeles, and shall have painted on the front of said
warehouse, in plain Roman letters at least ten inches in length, the words, ‘Storage
of Powder, Gasoline and Combustibles.”

Sec. 10. All buildings hereafter erected within the limits of District No. 1, of
the general Fire Limits of the City of Los Angeles, and’ all additions and enlarge-
ments thereof, shall have their outside walls and party walls made of brick, stone or
other incombustible material. Such outside walls and party walls shall extend from
the foundation to the top, and through the roof of said building. All roofs shall be
covered with such material as will afford protection against fire, and the party wall
shall pass through the roof in such manner as to break entirely any communication
of wood whatever between such roof and any other building. The term building in
this section shall not include privies or water closets. . The footing or base course
under all foundation walls shall be stone or hard brick, and shall be at least twice
the width of the bottom course of the foundation walls. All foundation walls mean
that portion of the wall below the level of the street curb. Outer walls are under-
stood hereby to be front, rear and two side walls. All walls shall be securely
anchored with iron anchors. No timbers shall be placed within six inches of any
flue, whether the same be a smoke, air, or any other flue. All openings for doors or
windows shall have a good and sufficient arch of stone or brick, well built and
keyed, or a lintel of stone or iron. No swelled or refused brick shall be allowed in
any wall or pier; no mortar made of lime and sand shall be used within 24 hours
after being mixed, and in all foundations cement ought to be used. All sand shall
be clean, sharp grit and free from loam, and all joints shall be entirely filled with
mortar. No cornice of wood shall be placed on any brick building in District No. L

of the Fire Limits.

Sec. 11. All bay windows which shall hereafter be erected in any building, shall
not project more than three feet; when flues are built in brick walls, the same shall
be carried two feet above the top of fire wall.

Sc. 12. It shall be and is unlawful for any person or persons, firm or. corpora-
tion, to erect a steam engine or boiler for any use, without first obtaining
permission of the city authorities, in the general Fire Limits of the City of Los
Angeles, and no:such permit shall be granted unless the person applying for the
same has filed a certificate signed by the manufacturer and a competent engineer,
who shall also be a competent boiler inspector, of the soundness of the same at the
date of the application for said permit.

Permits must be given only during the pleasure of the city authorities, and
must be constructed and then maintained to the satisfaction of the Chief of the Fire
Department.

ORDINANCE No. 49.

An ORDINANCE of the City of Los Angeles, relating to the regulation, sale and dis:
tribution of water and zanjas of the city for irrigating purposes. us

The Mayor and Couneil of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

SEcrion 1, The following is the price of water for irrigating inside the city —
limits, to-wit:

For one day, two (2) dollars per head.

For one half day, one dollar and twenty-five ($1.25) cents per head.

For one night, one dollar and twenty-five ($1.25) cents per head.

\


===== PDF PAGE 139 = PRINTED PAGE 139 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 139

For one hour, fifty (50) cents per head.
One day shall be regarded as from sunrise to sunset.

» Sec. 2. The Zanjero shall reserve one head of water on every zanja between
the hours of 12 m. and sunset of Thursday of each week, in order to supply persons
desiring water by the hour.

Src. 3. All persons desiring hour water on any zanja, shall apply for the same
at least three days prior to the Thursday for which application is made, and the,
Zanjero shall, on said Thursday, distribute the water to applicants therefor, in the
order of their applications. If any of said water remains unsold on said Thursday,
the Zanjero shall sell the same in the order for which it is applied, at the same rate;
provided, however, that the Zanjero shall not grant more than one hour’s water on
any zanja to any one person, if by so doing, others who have applied within the
time specified shall be deprived thereof.

Sec. 4. If at any time there shall be a surplus of water unsold at the times
specified in the ordinances of said city, providing for the time of applying for water
for irrigating purposes, the Zanjero may grant the use of the several zanjas of said
city for the purpose of carrying water through the same to persons residing outside
the limits of said city for the following prices, to-wit:

For the use of any zanja or part thereof carrying one head of water for one day, -
four (4) dollars. ;

For one day, two (2) dollars.

For the use of any zanja carrying two beads, for one day, eight (8) dollars.

For one night, four (4) dollars.

Nothing herein contained shall be construed as a relinquishment on the part of
the city to fully control the disposition of the use of the waters of Los, Angeles river
for irrigating purposes.

Src. 5. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordinance,
and shall cause the same to be published once in English in the Los Angeles daily
HERD, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of the
City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of January 21st, A. D. 1882.

ORDINANCE No. 51.

An ORDINANCE of the City of Los Angeles relating to the assessment and collection
of city taxes.

The. Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

Section I.

The fiscal year of the City of Los Angeles shall commence on the first day of
March of each year, and conclude at the end of the last day of February of each suc- ,
ceeding year.

(

Section IT.

All property within the corporate limits of the City of Los 5 aoe must be
assessed at its full cash value.

Section III.

The City Assessor must, between the beginning of,each fiscal year, on the first

day of March, and the first day of July following in each year, ascertain the names
of all taxable inhabitants and all the property within the corporate limits subject to
taxation, and must assess such property to the persons who are the owners thereof,
when known, and when the owner is unknown, then to unknown owners,

Szction IV.

He must exact from each person a statement in writing showing separately:
First—All property belonging to, claimed by, or in the possession or under the control
or management of such person. Second—All property belonging to or claimed by or
in the possession or under the control or management of any firm of which such
person is a member. Third—All property belonging to, claimed by, or in the
possession or under the control or management of any corporation of which such
person is President, Secretary, Cashier or Managing Agent. Fourth—An exact
description of all lands, improvements and personal property, and deposits of money,
gold dust or bullion, and the names of the persons with whom such deposits are
made, and the place in which they may be found; all mortgages, deeds of trust,
contracts and other obligations by which a debt is secured and the property
in the city affected thereby. Fifth—All”solvent cuedits unsecured by deed of”
trust, mortgage or other lien on real or personal property due or otving to such |
person or any firm of which he is a member, or due or owing to any corporation of
which he is President, Secretary, Cashier or Managing Agent, deducting from the

sum total of such credits such debts only unsecured by trust deed, mortgage oY
other lien on real or personal property as may be owing by such person, firm on ar

  


===== PDF PAGE 143 = PRINTED PAGE 143 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 143

corporation to bona fide residents of this State. No debt shall be so deducted unless
the statement shows the amount of such: debt as stated under oath in aggregate;
provided, in case of banks the statement is not required to show the debt in detail
or to whom it is owing; but the City Assessor shall have the privilege of eXamining
the books of said banks to verify said statement. | Whenever one member of a firm
or one of the proper officers of a corporation has a made a statement showing the
property of the firm or corporation, another member of the firm or another officer
need not include such property in the statement made by him; but his statement
must show the name of the person or officer who made the statement in which such
property is included.

The Council of said city must furnish the City Assessor with blank forms for

the statements provided for in this section, affixing thereto an affidavit which must
be substantially as follows:

i , do swear that the above list contains a full and correct statement of
all property subject to taxation which I, or any firm of which I am a member, or
any corporation, association or company of which I am President, Cashier, Secre-
tary or Managing Agent, owned, claimed, possessed or controlled at 12 o’clock m. on
the first Monday in March last, and which is not already assessed this year, and
that I have not in any manner whatsoever transferred or disposed of any property,
or placed any property out of the City of Los Angeles, or my possession, for the
purpose of avoiding any assessment upon the same or of making this statement;
and that the debts therein stated as owing by me are owing to bona fide residents of
this State, or firms or corporations doing business in this State.

The affidavit to the statement on behalf of a firm or corporation must state the
principal place of business of the firm or corporation, and in other respects must
conform substantially to the preceding form.

 

SEcTION V.

The City Assessor may fill out the statement at the time he presents it, or he
may deliver it to the person and require him, within an appointed time, to return
the same to him properly filled out.

Section VI.

The City Assessor shall have the same power and shall be vested with the same
authority as is provided in section 3632 of the Political Code in reference to making
assessments; provided, however, that one-half of all moneys recovered by the
Assessor under the provisions of said section 3632 must be by him paid to the City
. Treasurer, and the other half may be retained by the Assessor for his own use.

Section VII.

If any person, after demand made by the City Assessor, neglects or refuses to
give under oath the statement herein provided for, or to comply with the require-
ments of this ordinance, the City Assessor must note the refusal on the Assessment
Book opposite his name, and must make an estimate of the value of the property of
such person, and the value so fixed by the City Assessor must not be reduced by the
Mayor and Council, sitting as a Board of Equalization.


===== PDF PAGE 144 = PRINTED PAGE 144 =====
144 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

 

Section VIII.

Whenever the City Assessor deems it necessary to obtain an accurate description
of any tract or lot of land in the corporate limits, he may require the owner or his
agent to furnish the same, with any title papers he may have in his possession; and
if, on demand, the owner or agent neglects or refuses to furnish the same, the City
Assessor may employ the City Surveyor or Engineer to make out a description of
the boundaries and location thereof, and a statement of the quantity of land therein,
and the expenses of such survey must be returned by the City Assessor to the
Mayor and Council, who must add’ the amount to the taxes asessed upon the
property, which amount so added must, when collected by the City Tax Collector,
be paid over to said City Surveyor or Engineer, taking duplicate receipts therefor,
one of which he shall return to the Council.

Secrion IX.

If the owner or claimant of any property not listed by another person is absent _
or unknown, the City Assessor must make an estimate of the value of said property.
If the name of the absent owner is known to the City Assessor, the property must be
assessed in his name; if unknown, the property must be assessed to unknown
owners; all personal property consigned for sale to any person within this city, from.
any place outside of the city, must be assessed as other property.

SEcTION X.

When a person is assessed as agent, bailee, guardian, executor or administrator,
his representative designation must be added to his name, and the assessment entered
on a separate line from his individual assessment.

Section. XI.

Money and property in litigation in possession of a County Treasurer, of a
Court, County Clerk or Receiver, must be assessed to such Treasurer, Clerk or
Receiver, and the taxes be paid thereon under the direction of the Court.

Section XII.

Any property wilfully concealed, removed, transferred or misrepresented by
the owner or agent thereof to evade taxation, upon discovery, must be assessed at
not exceeding ten times\its value, and the assessment so made must not be reduced.
by the Mayor and Council, sitting as a Board of Equalization,

Any property discovered by the Assessor to have escaped assessment for the.
last preceding year, if such property is in the ownership or under the control of the
same person who owned or controlled it for such preceding year, may be assessed at
double its value.

Srcrion XIII.

The Council shall furnish the City Assessor an Assessment Book, with appro-
priate headings, alphabetically arranged, in which must be listed all property —
within the city, and in which must be specified, in separate columns, under the
appropriate head:

  


===== PDF PAGE 145 = PRINTED PAGE 145 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 145

The name of the person to whom the property is assessed.

Lands by metes and bounds or other description sufficient to identify it, giving

As soon as completed, the assessment book, together with the map book and

Ssecrion XVI.

Lands once described on the assessment book need not be described a second
time, but any person claiming the same and desiring to be assessed therefor, may have
his name inserted with that of the person to whom such land is assessed.

Section XVII. |

The Mayor and Council shall meet at the city council-room on the 15th day of
July in each year, as a Board of Equalization, to examine the assessment book and
equalize the assessment of property in the city, and shall continue in session from
day to day until the business of equalization is disposed of, but not later than the
5th day of August.

Section XVIII.

The Board ‘has power, after giving notice in such manner as it may by rule pre-
scribe, to increase or lower the entire assessment roll, or any assessment contained
therein, so as to equalize the assessment of the property contained in said roll, and
make the assessment conform to the true value of such property in money.

Srcrion XIX.

No reduction must be made in the valuation of property unless the party
‘affected thereby, or his agent, makes and files with the Board a written application
therefor, verified by his oath, showing the facts upon which it is claimed such reduc:
tion should be made. Before the Board grants the application or makes any reduc:
tion applied for, it must first examine on oath the person or the agent making the
application, touching the value of the property of such person. No reduction must
be made unless such person, or the agert making the application, attends and
answers all questions pertinent to the inquiry. Upon the hearing of the application,
the Board may subpena such witnesses, hear and take such evidence in relation to
the subject pending, as in its discretion it may deem proper.

will be investigated.

Section L.

Such deed, duly acknowledged or proved, is (except as against actual fraud)

States, the State, the county or the city, in which case it is prima facie evidence of

Srctron LI.

The assessment book or delinquent list, or a copy thereof, certified by the Clerk
of the Council, showing unpaid taxes against any person or property, is prima facie
evidence of the assessment, the property assessed, the delinquency, the amount of
taxes due and unpaid, and that all the forms of law in relation to the assessment
and levy of such taxes have been complied with.

the same, and if found correct, shall approve the same, and upon the approval
thereof, the Auditor shall make the proper entries in his books in regard thereto.

run wires over and along the public streets and thoroughfares within the limits of

Src. 2. Such poles so erected and to be erected shall be placed fifty yards
apart, unless otherwise ordered by the Council of said city, and within and adjoiming
the curb, where streets are sidewalked, when not otherwise directed by said Council,

-and upon all other streets and thoroughfares at such points as may be designated by

said Council, which Council shall have supervision over the location, under this
ordinance, of all poles to be erected by said company, said Council to have the right
to remove or cause to be removed any of the poles or wires of said company

ORDINANCE No. 55.

AN ORDINANCE relating to streets and sidewalks in the City of Los Angeles and to
obstructions thereon.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. No person or business firm shall use any portion of the sidewalks
in any part of the City of Los Angeles for any purpose whatever, excepting only for
the display of goods, wares land merchandise: and for the purpose of displaying
goods two feet in width—commencing at the front of the lot—may be used; provided,
that mefchants and others receiving and delivering goods shall be allowed twelve
hours from the time they are deposited until they are removed, and provided further
that a space of six feet in width shall at all times be kept clear for accommodation of
persons passing, and under no circumstances will anything be allowed to remain on
a sidewalk not over six feet wide, and in no case shall anything be placed or
permitted to remain in, on, over or along any gutter in front of any sidewalk in said
city.

Sec. 2. All awning constructed or placed over sidewalks shall be at least ten
feet above the walks.

Src. 3. No drop-curtains shall be used within the streets or alleys of the City


===== PDF PAGE 164 = PRINTED PAGE 164 =====
 

164 ORDINANCES -AND RESOLUTIONS

of Los Angeles, except for the purpose of shielding sidewalks and houses from rain —
or rays of the sun. \

Sze. 4. All water conductors leading from the roofs of houses into the streets
shall be continued down to the outer edge of the sidewalks.

See. 5. It shall be unlawful for any person or business firm to suspend or place, —
or have suspended or placed, over or across any sidewalk, street or alley within said —
city, any signboard or framework, cloth or other substance bearing the letters or
figures of a sign; provided, however, that above or along awnings or porches or —
piazas, signs may be displayed; but in no case shall signs be permitted below such
awnings, porches or piazas.

Suc. 6. Any person or persons having such signs or frames bearing signs, as —
prohibited in section 5 hereof, shall remove or cause,the same to be removed within —
thirty days from the first publication of this ordinance. °

Suc. 7. It shall be unlawful for any person or persons to throw papers of any —
kind into the streets of said city, or on the sidewalks thereof, or to throw or deposit —
any waste papers, poster, bill, advertisement, carcase of any dead animal, ‘filth or
any other substance whatever on any street or sidewalk of said city.

Sec. 8. Any person or persons violating any of the provisions of this ordinance
shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and on conviction therecf shall be pun-
ished by imprisonment in the county jail not exceeding sixty days, or by fine not
exceeding two hundred dollars, or by both fine and imprisonment.

Suc. 9. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordinance,
‘and cause the same to be published once in English in the Daily Heraxo, and
thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of the
City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of June 3d, A. D. 1882.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

RESOLUTION No. 93.

A Resotutron of the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles providing for
the laying out and constructing of a main branch public sewer, to be known as
the “Spring street Sewer.”

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, as follows:

SECTION 1. That there be and is hereby ordered to be laid out and constructed,
a main branch public sewer of said city, to be known and designated as the ‘‘Spring
street Sewer,” along and over the following-described route, to-wit:

Commencing at a point in center line of Spring street, where the same intersects
the center line of Temple street; thence southerly along the center line of Spring
street to where the same intersects the center Jine of Serenth street, a distance of
about 4,800 feet, as per map and profile in the: office of the City Surveyor for Los
Angeles city.

The said sewer is to be constructed of either cement pipe or of glazed burnt
clay pipe, or of brick, 1500 feet of which, from Temple street to Second street, shall be
of the inner diameter of eight inches in the clear, and 1320 feet of which, from Sec-
ond street to Fourth street, of the inner diameter of ten inches in the clear; and
1320 feet of which, from Fourth street to Sixth street, of the inner diameter of
twelve inches in the clear; and 660 feet of which, from Sixth to Seventh street, of
the inner diameter of fourteen inches in the clear; and to be constructed according
to the plans and specifications in the office of City Surveyor for Los Angeles City.

ORDINANCE No. 57.

An ORDINANCE relating to the distribution of water among certain owners of lands
on the Feliz Rancho.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

SEcrion 1. That the following-named persons, parties to the action entitled
Feliz et al vs. the City of Los Angeles, and recently decided by the Supreme Court
of the State of California,-may have the use of the water of the Los Angeles river for
irrigating and domestic purposes at such times and in such manner as hereinafter i
provided: S. W. Darby, Anasticao Feliz, Edward Partridge, Jesse Hunter, William .
Hunter and Amanda Crawford, and it is hereby ordained:

Sxc. 2. That said named parties owning land on said river may be allowed the
use of the waters of said river for irrigating and domestic purposes, next after the
inhabitants of the City of Los Angeles are supplied, and before any other land
outside of said city which does not border on the banks of said river and above said
city.

 


===== PDF PAGE 177 = PRINTED PAGE 177 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES, Ve

Sec. 3, The said named persons, and their heirs and assigns, as to their said
land on said river, shall be subject to the control and regulations of the city in their
use of the waters by the resolutions and ordinances of the governing body of said
city in regard to the same, and the said parties shall apply to the Zanjero or Water
Overseer of said city, on the 28th day of each month, or on such other day as may
hereafter by ordinance be prescribed, for a permit to use the water in the succeeding
month, and if at that time there is water not applied for, for the succeeding month,
shall take the water for Une purposes, at the times fixed in such permit and at
no other time.

Sec. 4. That said persons shall keep the Feliz ditch or such other ditches as
they may use for irrigating purposes in repair at their own expense, and they shall
have the use of the waters of said river, through said ditches and as hereinbefore
stated, free of charge, but under the regulations of the authorities of said city as
aforesaid.

Sec. 5. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this
ordinance, and cause the same to be published once in English in the Los Angeles
Daily HERALD, a newspaper published in the City of Los Angeles, and there-
upon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of the
City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of August 26th, A. D. 1882.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Approved this 29th day of August, A. D. 1882.
J. R. TOBERMAN,

Mayor.

changed or altered, the bed of the road and the tracks thereof shall be made to con-
form therewith.

any distance along said road exceed the sum of five cents for one fare, and the owner
or owners shall pay each year such a license to said city upon each car, as may be
required by ordinance of said city. f

the present limits of Main street—for the purpose of widening said Main street;

ORDINANCE No. 62.

Aw ORDINANCE prohibiting houses of prostitution and ill-fame in the City of Los
Angeles. a

 

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

Section 1. It shall be unlawful for any person to open, keep, maintain or ~
carry on within the limits of the City of Los Angeles, any bawdy house or place of
ill fame or prostitution, or to reside or live in any such house of ill-fame or prostitu-
tution for the purpose of carrying on or assisting in carrying on the business or
practice of fornication or prostitution. :

Sec. 2. Any act in violation of this ordinance, for each day of its continuance
shall jbe considered as a separate offense. Every person who violates any of the
provisions of this ordinance is guilty of a misdemeanor, and is punishable by impris-
onment in the county jail not exceeding sixty days, or by fine not exceeding two
hundred dollars, or by both.

Sec. 3. All ordinances or parts of ordinances conflicting with the provisions of
this ordinance are hereby repealed. . 4

Sec. 4. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordinance, 4
and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily Heraup.
and thereupon and thereafter the same shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles, at its session of November 11th, A. D. 1882.
W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.
Approved this 13th day of November, A. D. 1882.
J. R. TOBERMAN,
Mayor.

First—Any quantity of hay of any kind exceeding three tons in weight.

Second—Any petroleum, gasoline or any product of petroleum or hydro-carbon
liquids, unless the same are kept in iron tanks, and in no larger quantity than one
hundred and fifty gallons.

Third—Any Hercules, dynamite, giant powder or any kind of blasting powder
or gun powder, in any quantity over fifty pounds.

Sec. 5. It shall-be and is unlawful for any person or persons, firm or corpora-
tion to store, permit the storage of, or keep for sale within the general Fire Limits
“of the City of Los Angeles, any reflned petroleum in larger quanties than two
hundred gallons, the same to be always kept in metal cans, and the said oil shall
stand a fire test of one hundred and ten (110) degrees Fahrenheit.

Sec. 6. It shall be and is unlawful for any person, persons, firm or corporation
to manufacture within the general Fire Limits of the City of Los Angeles, any acids
or any, other combustible or explosive chemicals, to boil or refine oils, or to manufac-
ture matches.

-

Sec. 7. No person shall use any portable light in any building or place where
combustible materials or hay is kept, unless such light be securely kept in a lantern.

Sec. 8. Each person making, using or having charge or control of shavings,
hay, straw, sacks, bags, litter or any other combustible waste or fragments, which
are generally accumulated in the yards of stores, the same shall be removed once in

_ every two weeks.

Sec. 9. All warehouses used for storage of any kind of powder, gasoline, crude
petroleum, or any product of petroleum which shall flash or emit an inflammable
a vapor at a temperature below 110° Fahrenheit, must be located outside the general
Fire Limits of the City of Los Angeles, and shall have painted on the front of said
warehouse, in plain Roman letters, at least ten inches in length, the words, ‘‘Storage

of Powder, Gasoline and Combustibles.”

Suc. 10: All buildings hereafter erected within the limits of District No. 1 of
the general Fire Limits of the City of Los Angeles, and all additions and enlarge-
ments thereof, shall have their outside walls and party and partition walls made of
brick, stone or other incombustible material. Such outside walls and party and
partition walls shall extend from the foundation to the top, and through the roof of
said building. All roofs shall be covered with such material as will afford protec-
tion against fire, and the party wall shall pass through the roof in such manner as to
break entirely any communication of wood whatever between such roof and any
other building. The term building in this section shall not include privies and
water closets. The footing or base course under all foundation walls shall be of
stone or hard brick, and shall be at least twice the width of the bottom course of the
foundation walls. ~All foundation walls mean that portion of the wall below the
level of the street curb.

Outer walls are understood hereby to be front, rear and two side walls.

All walls shall be securely anchored with iron anchors. No timber shall be
_ ‘placed within six inches of any flue, whether the same be a smoke, air or any other
' flue. All openings for doors or windows shall have a good and sufficient arch of


===== PDF PAGE 203 = PRINTED PAGE 202 =====
202 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  

stone or brick, well built and keyed, or a lintel of stone or iron. No swelled or
refuse brick shall be allowed in any wall or pier; no mortar made of lime and sand
shall be used within twenty-four hours after being mixed, and in all foundations
cement ought to be used. All sand shall be clean, sharp grit, and free from loam,
and all joints shall be entircly filled with mortar. No cornice of wood shall be
placed in any brick building in District No. 1 of the Fire Limits.

Sxc. 11. All bay windows which shall hereafter be erected in any building, s
shall not project more than three feet; when flues are built in brick walls the same
shall be carried two feet above the top of the fire wall.

Sxc. 12. It shall be and is unlawful for any person or persons, firm or corpora-
tion to erect a steam engine or boiler for any use, without first obtaining the per. ~
mission of the city authorities in the general Fire Limits of the City of Los Angeles, iN
and no such permit shall be granted unless the person applying for the same has
filed a certificate, signed by the manufacturer and a competent engineer, whoishall
also be a competent boiler inspector, of the soundness of the same at the date of the
application for said permit.

Permits must be given only during the pleasure of the city authorities, and
must be constructed and then maintained to the satisfaction of the Chief of the Fire
Department.

 

Src. 13. All buildings hereafter erected to be used for public assemblages, in
whole or in part, shall have the doors constructed to open both inwardly and out-
wardly, andiin no ease shall they be constructed to open inwardly only, or to slide.

And all buildings now in use should be made to conform to this section.

Sec. 14. Spark catchers shall be placed upon all chimneys or smoke stacks,
whenever deemed necessary for the safety of adjoining buildings, and so ordered by
a majority of the City Council.

 

Sec. 15. All vats, tanks and receptacles used by parties to light their prem-
ises, whether for naptha or gasoline, must be placed at least four feet below the
surface of the natural grade of the street.

   
   
   
    
 

Src. 16. It shall be and is unlawful for any person, persons, firm or corpora-
tion engaged in selling oils, to mix or adulterate any oils used for illuminating pur-
poses with benzine, naptha, gasoline, or any other substance, and all oils from
petroleum or its products shall stand a fire test of 110° Fahrenheit.

Suc. 17. It shall be unlawful for any person to ignite, set fire to or burn any
paper, shavings, boxes or other things upon any street, sidewalk or lots within the
limits of District No. 1 of the general Fire Limits, or carry any lighted candle,
taper or lamp, or have the ‘same so lighted within ten feet of any inflammable or
combustible powder or liquid kept or stored within the limits of District No. lof
the general Fire Limits of said city.

Suc. 18. Any person, persons, firm or corporation who'shall violate, neglect or
refuse to comply with any provision of this ordinance, shall be deemed guilty of By
misdemeanor, and on conviction thereof, shall be fined not less than $50 nor more

than $200, or by imprisonment in the jail not less than twenty-five days, nor more
than one hundred days, or by both such fine and imprisonment.

Sec. 19. All ordinances and parts of ordinances in conflict with this ordinance,
and all resolutions and parts of resolutions in conflict with this ordinance, are here-
by repealed.

Sec. 20. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordinance,
and cause the-same to be published in the Los Angeles Daily Hrranp, and

RESOLUTION No. 122.

A RESoLUTION of the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, providing for
the improvement and grading of Third street, between Main and Spring

streets.
_ Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, as follows:

Section 1. That the following improvements, at the expense of the property
owners, shall be made on Third street, between Main and Spring streets:

The road-bed shall be graded and covered with eight inches of gravel, raked
free of coarse stoges of more than two inches in diameter, and it shall be made to
conform to the established grade at the center of the street, with the proper slope
toward the curb. After being graveled, it shall be thoroughly wet and then rolled.

The curb shall be of redwood 3x12 inches, placed with the top to the established
grade, and spiked to posts of redwood 4x4 inches three feet long, set into the ground
full length-below the top of the curb and inside of the same, and not more than four
_ feet apart, with one to each joint of the curbing.

The sidewalks shall be nine feet wide, graded and covered with three inches of
fine gravel, smoothly laid, and raked free from coarse stones of more than one inch
in diameter. The slope of the sidewalks shall be three inches toward the curb.

Src. 2. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this resolution,
‘and shall cause the same to be published in the Los Angeles Daily HrEraxp,
" a newspaper published in said city, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect

and be in force.

RESOLUTION No. 124.

A Resonution of the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, providing
regulations for hacks, job wagons, trucks, drays, etc., and for public stands for

the same.

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles as follows:

Section 1. Every vehicle except railroad cars, which shall be used for the con:
veyance of persons by land from place to place, for hire, shall be deemed a hackne
carriage within the meaning of this resolution.


===== PDF PAGE 206 = PRINTED PAGE 205 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 205

 

. Sec. 2. Every vehicle which shall be used for the conveyance of goods pack-
ages or freight from place to place in this city, for hire (except andecants and
except, also, the vehicles used by merchants, dealers and manufacturers erclueively
for the delivery of their-wares to customers), shall be deemed a job wagon within
the meaning of this resolution.

Sec. 8. Every vehicle which shall be used for the conveyance of wood, vegeta-
bles, farm products, or other merchandise intended for sale, shall be deemed a
market wagon within the meaning of this resolution,

Sec. 4, Los Angeles street, between Commercial and Arcadia streets, is hereby
designated as a public stand for the use of market wagons used for the conveyance
of hay.
~ Los Angeles street, between First and Requena streets, is hereby designated as

a public stand for the use of market wagons used for the conveyance of wood.

is For the use of all other market wagons not included in the two foregoing clauses,
and for the use of all hackney carriages and job wagons, the streets surrounding the
public plaza, east of Main street and north of the Pico House, are hereby designated
as a public stand; provided, that said last aforesaid public stand shall extend from
the outer edge of the fence surrounding said plaza only thirty feet outward; and
provided further, that nothing in this resolution’ shall prevent the Council of the
City of Los Angeles from establishing, at any time, by resolution, other public
stands within the meaning of this resolution. y

Sec. 5. In addition to the foregoing public stands, the following places are
* hereby designated as lawful stands for hackney carriages in this city, to-wit: In
front of each hotel in this city, whether the ground floor of the building in which
such hotel is conducted be included as part thereof or not; provided, that not more
than two hackney carriages shall be permitted to stand at the main front entrance
of any hotel at the same time. The carriages to be designated by the party or
parties having charge of such hotel; and provided further, that the regular passenger
coach of such hotel may stand in front thereof at any and all times.

Src. 6. No person having charge of any hackney carriage, job wagon or market
wagon shall allow the same to stand within ten feet of any crossing, nor at any
greater distance than two feet from the outer edge of any sidewalk.

Sec. 7. No person having the charge or control of any hackney carriage,
job wagon or market wagon, shall occupy as a stand for the same, any portion
of any street in front of any building or vacant lot, where the width of such street is
fifty feet or less, or where the owner of such building or vacant lot or the occupant
of the’street floor of such building shall object; provided, that nothing herein con-
tained shall be so construed as to deprive any party or parties having charge\or
management of any hotel, of the right to designate and permit hackney carriages to
stand in front thereof, as provided in section 5 of this resolution; and provided
further, that nothing in this resolution shall prevent any owner or driver of any
hackney carriage from stopping at any place other than a crossing, for the purpose of
taking up or putting down a passenger or passengers with their baggage, in whose
service such hackney carriage may at the time be actually employed; and provided

further, that nothing in this resolution shall prevent the owner or driver of any job
wagon or market wagon from stopping at any place other than a public crossing ft
any public street, from one sidewalk to another, for the purpose of receiving or de:

livering any goods, wares or merchandise; and provided further, that hackney ~

carriages and job wagons may stand in front of real property owned or rented by the
owner of said hackney carriages or wagons, on streets more than fifty feet wide.

Src. 8. Whenever several hackney carriages shall attend at any place for or
with passengers, the Chief of Police, or any regular or special policeman may give
directions respecting the standing of such carriages while waiting for, taking up or —
putting down passengers, and every driver of such carriage shall conform to and
comply with such directions.

Szc. 9. All persons are hereby prohibited from using any part of the streets of
the City of Los Angeles as a stand or stopping place for any hacks, hackney car-
riages, coaches, job wagons, trucks, drays or other vehicles, except hereinbefore

provided,

Sxc. 10. Any person violating, refusing or neglecting to comply with the pro-
visions of this resolution, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and shall, on conviction,
be fined not less than five dollars, nor more than thirty dollars, or be imprisoned in
the county jail not less than two days, nor more than ten days, or by both such fine
and imprisonment.

Src. 11. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this resolution,

and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in full force, and all
ordinances, resolutions, rules and regulations, or parts of the same, in so far as they
may be inconsistent with this resolution, shall be and the same are hereby repealed.

I hereby certify that the foregoing resolution was adopted by the Council of the
City of-Los Angeles, at its regular meeting of January 27th, A. D. 1883.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

SgcTion 1. Every person (except a California Indian) without visible means of
living, who has the physical ability to work, and who dees not for the space of ten
days seek employment nor labor when employment is offered him; every healthy

beggar who solicits alms as a business; every person who roams about from place to
place without any lawful business; every idle or dissolute person or associate of
known thieves, who wanders about the streets at late or unusual hours of the night,
or who lodges in any barn, shed, shop, out-house, vessel or place other than such as
is kept for lodging purposes, without the permission of the owner or party entitled
to the possession thereof; every lewd and dissolute person, who lives in and about
houses of ill-fame, and every common prostitute and common drunkard, is a vagrant,
and punishable by imprisonment in the city jail not exceeding ninety days, or by a
fine not exceeding ninety dollars, or by both such fine and imprisonment, and in
ease of sentence of imprisonment, the court may make it a part of the judgment and
sentence that the person so sentenced shall perform labor in the chain gang of said
city, during the time of said imprisonment.

ORDINANCE No. 70.

An Orpuvance establishing water rates and fixing the compensation for water to be
furnished by any person, company or corporation for family uses, for private
purposes, for municipal uses-and for all public purposes in the City of Lo:

_ Angeles, for the year commencing July Ist, 1883.

~The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Srection 1. The monthly rates of compensation to be collected by any person,
company or corporation engaged in the business of supplying water to the inhabit-
ants of the City of Los Angeles for domestic purposes, for private purposes, for
municipal purposes and for all public purposes of said city, for the year commencing
July Ist, 1883, and ending June 30th, 1854, are hereby fixed as follows:

For tenements, including for bath tub, occupied by a single family—

For one-story buildings, $1.50.
For two-story buildings, $2.
For three-story buildings, $2.50.
Horses kept for private use, including water for washing one vehicle, for each

: horse, 25c.

And for eich additional horse, 124c.

_ And for each additional vehicle, 12c.

_ For hose for washing windows, sidewalks, gardens or grounds, for every lot not
nore than 60 feet front, 50c; 60 to 100 feet front, $1; over 100 feet front, 2 cents
per front foot for all over 100 feet, in addition to the rate for the 100 feet.

For each water closet used in private houses, 25c.
For each water closet used in public buildings, $2.
For each urinal used in private buildings, 25c.

For each urinal used in public buildings, $1.


===== PDF PAGE 214 = PRINTED PAGE 213 =====
 

OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 213

For water furnished for building purposes, for each barrel of lime used, 20c.

For bakeries, for each barrel of flour, 5c.

Stores, banks, offices, warehouses, saloons, groceries, barber shops, butcher
shops, blacksmith shops, book binderies, confectioners, churches, halls, laundries,
photograph galleries, printing offices, steam engines, greenhouses, markets, market
stores, horse troughs, soda fountains, and other places of business not supplied by
meter, to be charged according to the éstimiated quantity used, from $1 to $10.

When meters are used, then, if the quantity used does not exceed 10,000 gallons
per month, for each 1000 gallons, $1; over 10,000 gallons per month, 75c for each
1000.

Hotels, taverns, boarding houses, boarding schools, lodging houses, in addition
to family rates, for each boarder or lodger, 10c.

For every bath-tub used in barber shops, bathing establishments and hotels,
$2.50.

Fountains shall be regulated by contract.

All persons, companies or corporations furnishing water as aforesaid, shall have
power in all cases to apply meters, at their own expense, for the purpose of discov-
ering waste or excessive use, and when waste or excessive use is found, to charge
meter rates.

For water required for purposes that are not specified in the above tariff, the
rates shall be in proportion to the above tariff where meters are not used, and the
meter rates when meters are used. 9

All water furnished for sprinkling streets, flushing sewers, watering parks, or
water used for the extinguishment of fires, shall be furnished free, provided, that
where the City of Los Angeles is not entitled by law or contract to water free for
the extinguishment of fires and sprinkling the streets, the rate on each hydrant used
for the extinguishment of fires shall be 20c. per month, and on each hydrant used
for sprinkling streets, $1 per month.

All rates, except meter rates, are due and payable in advance, and meter rates
are due and payable at the end of the month, and upon meter rates a deposit not
exceeding three-fourths (?) of the value of the estimated quantity of water to be
consumed for the month may be required.

and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily Hzraxp, a

ORDINANCE No. 71.

AN Orprnance of the City of Los Angeles, providing for the construction and re-
pairing of the sidewalks on certain streets.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

Secrion 1. That hereafter all sidewalks of such portions of the following
streets of said city as are hereinafter described, shall be constructed only of asphal-
tum or smooth stones, viz: :

On both sides of Main street, from the north line of Second street to a point on
Main street, north of the Pico House and opposite to the center of the plaza.

On both sides of Spring street, from the north line of Second street to the south
line of Temple street.

On both sides of Los Angeles street, from the north side of First street to the
south side of Arcadia street.

On both sides of First street, between Los Angeles street and Fort street.

On both sides of Requena street, between Main street and Wilmington strees,

On both sides of Commercial street, between Main street and Alameda street.

On hoth sides of Arcadia street, between Main street and Los Angeles street.

On both sides of Temple street, from Spring street to Buena Vista street.

On both sides of Turner street, between Main Street and New High street.

On both sides of Court street, between Main street and Spring street.

On both sides of Market street, between Main street and Spring street.

Sec. 2. All owners of real property on all graded streets in said city are hereby
required to construct and keep in good order all sidewalks in front of their property;
provided, that gravel sidewalks upon streets or parts of streets other than those
mentioned in section one (1) of this ordinance, shall be repaired by being filled to
the established grade with fine, sharp gravel, properly leveled, and no part of the
gravel in any case shall exceed one inch in diameter, and all stones one inch or
more in diameter on said sidewalks shall be removed therefrom or broken into a
size not exceeding one inch in diameter, before such filling; and all brush and weeds
shall be removed before such filling.

Src. 3. Whenever the sidewalks in front of any real property in the City of
Los Angeles are out of repair, the Board of Public Works shall, by a written notice,
notify the owner or owners of said property to repair the said sidewalks, or shall
notify them to construct new sidewalks within ten days after the service of the
notice. The said notice shall specify the manner in which the sidewalks are to be
repaired or constructed, and the material to be used therein.

Sze. 4. Hereafter no sidewalks in the City of Los Angeles, upon the streets or
parts of streets described in section one (1) of this ordinance, shall be repaired or
constructed, unless such repairs or sidewalks so constructed shall be made of smooth
stone or asphaltum, and the further repairs on the sidewalks upon the streets and
parts of streets described in said section are hereby prohibited, unless said repairs
or alterations be made in smooth stone or asphaltum.

Whenever any sidewalk composed of any material other than smooth stone or


===== PDF PAGE 216 = PRINTED PAGE 215 =====
 

 

OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 215

asphaltum, which has heretofore been constructed upon any of the steets or parts of
streets described in section one of this ordinance, shall be in need of repairs, the
owner of property upon which such sidewalks so in need of repairs front, shall con-
struct new sidewalks in front of such property, of smooth stone or asphaltum.

Sec. 5. In case the said owner or owners of the said property shall fail to repair
or construct the said sidewalks within the said ten days, as hereinbefore provided,
after due notice given, the Board of Public Works may cause the same to be re-
paired or constructed at the expense of the said owner or owners, and the amount so
expended for constructing or repairing sidewalks in front of said real property, as
hereinbefore provided, shall be a personal charge against the person or persons
owning the said property, and may be recovered by the City of Los Angeles, by
action in the Courts, against such person or persons. And for every neglect to
comply with the terms of this ordinance, the owner of the said property shall for-
feit and pay to the City of Los Angeles the sum of fifty dollars, and the further
penalty of ten dollars for each day during which such neglect continues, to be re-
covered from the owner or owners of said property.

Src. 6. Any one violating the provisions of this ordinance, and any one failing
to repair or construct sidewalks after due notice given, within the time and in the
manner specified in the notice therefor, as hereinbefore provided, shall be guilty of
a misdemeanor, and be fined not less than ten dollars nor more than fifty dollars,
or be imprisoned not less than ten days nor more than fifty days in the city jail;
and every additional day during which any person shall fail to repair or construct
sidewalks, after due notice given, within the time and in the manner specified in
the notices therefor, as hereinbefore provided, shal] constitute an additional offense
and be punishable as herein specified.

Sec. 7. All ordinances and parts of ordinances, and all resolutions and parts
of resolutions, so far as they conflict with this ordinance, and no farther, are hereby
repealed.

The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordinance, and
cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily Hrratp, and
thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of the
City of Los Angeles, at its regular meeting of March 3d, A. D. 1883.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Approved this 5th day of March, A. D. 1883.
C. E. THOM,

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles:

Section 1. That the following improvements, at the expense of the property |
owners, shall be made on Olive strect, between Temple and Covrt House streets;

The road-bed shall be graded and covered with eight inches of gravel. Along
the crown of the street it shall be four inches above the grade of the west curb of
the street, with such a slope toward the curbs that at the outside of the gutters it
shall be ten inches below the grade of the respective curbs. After being graveled,
it shall be thoroughly wet and then rolled. ‘There shall be no stones in said gravel
larger than two inches in diameter.

The gutters shall be 35 feet wide and paved with granite cobble stones not
less than eight inches long, thoroughly set in sand and then rammed. The center
of the gutters shall be fourteen inches, and the outside adjoining the road-bed and
the curbs shall be ten inches below the grade of the respective curbs.

The curb shall be of redwood, 3x12 inches, placed with the top to the estab-
lished grade, spiked to posts of redwood, 4x4 inches, three feet long, set into the
ground full length below the top of the curb and inside of the same, and not more
than four feet apart, with one at each joint in the curbing.

The sidewalks shall be twelve feet wide, graded and covered with three inches of
fine gravel, smoothly laid and raked free from coarse stones of more than one inch in
diameter. The slope of the sidewalks shall be three inches toward the curb.

Sxc. 2. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this resolution,
and shall cause the same to be published once inthe Los Angeles Daily Hrratp,
a newspaper published in said city, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect
and be in force. )

ORDINANCE No. 72.

An OrpINANce providing for the forcing of criminals to work on the streets and
other public works of the City of Los Angeles.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

SEctIon 1. That in all cases of the entry of a judgment against any person for
any violation of the ordinances of the City of Los Angeles, wherein the said persons
shall be sentenced to pay a fine, the Court shall have power to make it a part of the
judgment that the defendant be imprisoned until the fine be paid and satisfied, ab
the rate of one dollar per day; and the Court may make it a part of the judgment

 


===== PDF PAGE 218 = PRINTED PAGE 217 =====
 

 

 

OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 207

and sentence that such person shall perform labor on the streets and other public
works of said city until such fine shall be discharged, at the rate of one dollar per
day. For each day which the said person so convicted may pass in prison, he shall
be entitled to a credit of one dollar upon his flne, and he may at any time pay the
sum then remaining unsatisfied and obtain his discharge from custody. And in all
eases Of the entry of judgment against any person for any violation of the ordinances
of the City of Los Angeles, wherein the said person shall be sentenced to imprison:
ment, the said person may be forced, and the Court may make it a part of the
judgment, that he be forced to perform labor on the streets and other public works
of said city, during the term of such imprisonment; provided, that in no case shall
any person under sixteen years of age, or any female, be forced to, work upon the
public works of said city.

Sec. 2. All ordinances and parts of ordinances, so far as they conflict with this
ordinance, but no further, shall be and the same are hereby repealed.

ORDINANCE No. 73.

An ORDINANCE regulating and providing for the punishment of keepers of disorderly
and riotous houses, and of persons guilty of disorderly conduct in their houses
or yards.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

Srction 1. Any person who shall keep a riotous or disorderly house, or suffer
any riotous or disorderly conduct in his house or yard connected with such house,
or shall be guilty of any riotous or disorderly conduct in any house, street or place,
whereby the peace, quiet or decency of the neighborhood of such house or of any
person may be disturbed, shall be punished by a fine of not less than ten nor more
than one hundred dollars, or by imprisonment not less than ten nor more than one
hundred days, or by both such fine and imprisonment.

Sec. 2. All ordinances and parts of ordinances in conflict with this ordinance
are hereby repealed.

ORDINANCE No. 74.

AN ORDINANCE of the City of Los Angeles, relating to the numbering of buildings,
and providing for the punishment of those who violate its provisions.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do erdain as follows:

Sxcrion 1. Ail entrances from the public streets of the City of Los Angeles to
buildings shall be numbered as hereinafter provided. The number of each and
every entrance shall be placed upon or immediately above the door or gate closing
said entrance, and each figure of said number shall be at least one inch and three-
quarters in height and of corresponding width. ‘The appropriate number of any
entrance to any building shall be placed thereon within five days after the receipt
by the owner, occupant, lessee, tenant or sub-tenant of such building, of a notice
trom the Board of Public Werks of said city, of the number or numbers designated
for such building, and all numbers other than the numbers provided for in this
ordinance for the respective entrances, shall be removed from every building by the
owners, occupants, lessees, tenants or sub-tenants thereof, within five days from the
service of the said notice designating the appropriate numbers to be placed thereon,

The Board of Public Works shall serve, or cause to be served, a written notice
upon the owner, occupant, lessce, tenant or sub-tenant of any building, containing
the number or numbers to be placed, within five days aiter the receipt of such
notice upon said building.

It shall be the duty of the City Surveyor to designate the respective starting
points for numbers to Le placed on, and also the respective numbers for, buildings
fronting on streets heretofore laid ont or hereafter to be laid out or extended. And
whenever the change or extension of any street shall necessitate a change in the
numbering of the buildings on said street, the City Surveyor shall designate the
proper number; the Board of Public Works shall have notices served as hereinbefore
provided, and.each person receiving such notice shall, within five days after the
service of such notice, make the required changes.

Sec. 2. The following skali he the respective starting points for numbers on
buildings fronting on streets heretofore laid out or hereafter to be laid out or ex-
tended, viz: Main street, including Upper Main street and San Fernando street, and
First street, or the nearest point to said streets, for all streets crossing, or running
from, or from the direction of said Main, Upper Main, San Fernando or First


===== PDF PAGE 221 = PRINTED PAGE 220 =====
220 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

streets; on those streets crossing Main, Upper Main and San Fernando, on the por-
tion of such streets east of Main, Upper Main or San Fernando streets, the buildings
are to be numbered the appropriate numbers east, and on those crossing First street
or the portion of such streets north of First street, the buildings are to be num-
bered the appropriate numbers north. The buildings on Main, Upper Main and
San Fernando streets are to be numbered as though said streets constituted one
continuous street.

Szc. 38. The numbers on the northerly and westerly sides of streets shall be
odd numbers, and the numbers on the southerly and easterly sides thereof shall be

even numbers.

Sec. 4. A block, within the meaning of this ordinance, shall be that portion of
any street between two cross streets, provided, that where a system of streets abut
on any street, the space between two of such abutting streets shall be considered a
block; in such cases the prolonged center line of the abutting street shall be the
dividing line of blocks; and provided further, Main and Spring streets, between
Temple and First streets, shall be considered two blocks each, and that Main street,
from Temple street and the extension of the center line thereof, to Marchessault
street, shall be considered two blocks.

Sec. 5. One hundred numbers, or as many thereof as may be necessary, shall
be allotted to each block, except the first block from each starting point, which shall
be allotted ninety-nine numbers, or as many thereof as may be necessary, numbers
100, 200 and 300 being respectively the numbers for commencing the blocks distant
one, two or three streets from the starting point on the side designated for even
numbers; and numbers 101, 201 and 301 in similar manner for the opposite side of
the street throughout its extent; so that the initial figure of a number placed on a
building the intersection of street shall indicate the number of blocks such cross-
ing is distant from the street used as a starting point.

Not less than twenty (20) feet in frontage of all vacant lots of ground shall be

allowed for each number.
On all cross or intermediate streets the numbering shall commence where the
streets begin, and shall conform to the above plan.

Src. 6. Any person, persons, firms or corporation who shall violate, neglect or
refuse to comply with any of the provisions’ of this ordinance, shall be deemed
guilty of a misdemeanor, and on conviction thereof shall be fined not less than ten
dollars, nor more than thirty dollars, or by imprisonment in the city jail not less
than ten days, nor more than thirty days, or by both such fine and imprisonment.

Src. 7. All ordinances and parts of ordinances, and all resolutions or parts of
resolutions, so far as they conflict with this ordinance, but no further, are hereby
repealed.

Suc. 8. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordinance,

and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily Hera,
and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

ORDINANCE No. 75.

An ORDINANCE providing for the punishment of any one who cuts an aperture in
any place where water is drawn out of the Los Angeles river, or injures or suf-

fers to injured, or obstructs or suffers to be obstructed, the flow of water in, or ~

who places any injurious substance in, any zanja or flume belonging to the City
of Los Angeles. .

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

Section 1. Any person who shall make or cause to be made any aperture in
any place where water is drawn out of the Los Angeles river, into a water canal of
the City of Los Angeles, or who shall make, cause or suffer to be made, any aperture
in any flume, wooden trough, ditch, canal, zanja or other water conduit belonging
to said city; who shall raise, or cause or suffer to be raised; destroy, cause or suffer
to be destroyed; break, cause or permit to be broken; cut, cause or suffer to be cut;
injure, cause or suffer to be injured; remove, cause or suffer to be removed, any
flume, wooden trough, ditch, canal, zanja or other water conduit belonging to said
city; shall place, cause or suffer to be placed, any obstruction to the course of water
in any flume, wooden trough, ditch, canal, zanja or other water conduit of said city, of
such a character as may injure the banks or sides or bottoms of the same, or render
the water therein unclean or unfit for use for drinking or irrigating purposes, shall
be guilty cf a misdemeanor, and shall be fined, on conviction, not less than ten nor
more than fifty dollars, or imprisoned not less than ten nor more than fifty days,
or by both such fine and imprisonment.

Sec. 2. All ordinances and parts of ordinances in conflict with this ordinance
are hereby repealed.

Sec. 8. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this
ordinance, and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
HERALD, and thereupon and thereafter it shall be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of the
City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of March 19th, A. D. 1888.

ORDINANCE No. 78.

 

An Orprnance to provide for the purchase of the necessary lands, and the construc:
tion of buildings thereon, and the furnishing of the same for a City Hall in and
for the City of Los Angeles, and thereunto establishing the necessary regula:
tions and rules of procedure.

 


===== PDF PAGE 226 = PRINTED PAGE 225 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. — 2s

hwo

5

Whereas, under and by virtue of the powers granted to the corporation of the

City of Los Angeles by section 2 of article 2, and section 1 of article 4, of the re-

"vised Charter of the City of Los Angeles, entitled ‘An Act to amend an Act en-
titled an Act to revise an Act entitled an Act to amend the Charter of the City of
Los Angeles, to define its limits and rights, to enlarge its powers and to provide for
its more efficient government,” approved March 30th, 1878, is the authority ‘‘to
hold and receive property, real and personal, or either, within or without the limits
of the said city, for any or all of the following purposes, to-wit:

“First.—For public buildings, public works and improvements, * * or
either.)

“Ninth.—For any and all other public or municipal objects as required for the
protection, benefit and convenience of said city and its imhabitants * *

“fo manage and control all city property * * *

“Yo provide for the arrangement and preservation of the records, papers and
archives of said city, and also to exercise and carry out and execute such other
powers and authority as is given to said corporation by this Act either expressly or
by implication and not otherwise specially delegated, and to make, pass and adopt
for such purposes such laws, rules and regulations as shall be necessary therefor.”

Whereas, it has become necessary for the best interests of the said city by the
better security and preservation of the city records, papers and archives, and in the
better economy of the city expenditures, to secure a City Hall, the property of said
city, wherein to have deposited all the records, papers and archives of the said city,
and wherein shall be located and appointed all rooms and offices of the city govern-
ment; and

Whereas, under the limitations of the Constitution of the State of California,
article XI, section 18, the moneys necessary to carry out this object are allowed to
be appropriated only upon a vote of the qualified electors of the said city, had at an
election thereunto called; now, therefore,

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Secrion 1. The City of Los Angeles, by the means hereinafter provided, and
for its own proper use and benefit, shall cause to be selected and purchased the
necessary lands, and thereupon to be erected, constructed and furnished, in accord-
ance with such plan as the Council of said city shall at any time after this ordinance
shall go into effect adopt, a suitable building, to be known and designated the City
Hall of the City of Los Angeles, to be used and occupied as the depository of all the
city records, papers and archives of the said city, and wherein shall be located all
the offices and rooms of the municipal government of the City of Los Angeles.

Sec. 2. For the purpose of carrying out the object of this ordinance, as in the
section last above specified, the Council of the City of Los Angeles is instructed and
authorized to issue the bonds of the said city to an amount not exceeding one
hundred thousand ($100,000) dollars, to be payable on or before the expiration of
twenty years from and after the date of their issuance, with interest thereon at the
rate of six per céntum per annum, payable semi-annually, on the first days of Janu-
ary and July in each year, both principal and interest to be made payable in U. S.

gold coin only. The bonds shall be issued in the denomination of one thousand ($1000)
dollars each, and shall be signed by the Mayor of the City of Los Angeles and the


===== PDF PAGE 227 = PRINTED PAGE 226 =====
226 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

Clerk of the Council of said city. Interest coupons shall be attached to said bonds, 4

signed by the City Treasurer of the City of Los Angeles. The City Council shall

issue all the said bonds from time to time, at such times as shall be necessary to ©
provide funds for the payment of the purchase price of lands and material, and the —

work of construction and furnishing, or either, for the prosecution of the work
hereinbefore specified.

Szc. 38. The bonds and coupons shall be payable at the office of the City

Treasurer; and all coupons, as soon as they are paid, shall be detached and canceled

by the City Treasurer, and by him, within one month thereafter, deposited with the
City Auditor of the said city, who will give the said Treasurer his receipt for any
such deposit of coupons. Every city bond issued pursuant to this ordinance shall bear
the date of its issuance, and upon the sale of any such bond the purchaser shall pay,
in addition to the purchase price of said bond, all accrued interest up to the date of
the sale thereof,

Src. 4. Before or at the time of the issuance of said bonds, the Council of the
Gity of Los Angeles shall, by a resolution adopted in accordance with the pro-

visions of the said City Charter regulating the passage of resolutions, make pro-

visions for the payment of the interest upon the said bonds as the same shall fall 4

due, and for the establishment of a sinking fund for the payment of the principal
when the same shall become due and payable.

Sec. 5, At any time within one month after this ordinance shall have gone
into effect, the Council of the City of Los Angeles, at any lawful meeting thereof,
may call a special election of the qualified electors of the City of Los Angeles, for
the purpose of voting upon the question of the issuance or non-issuance of the bonds
hereinbefore provided for, within the meaning of article XI, section 18, of the Con-
stitution of the State of California, which election shall be called, held, conducted
and declared in all respects as provided in article X of the said City Charter; and

the words to appear upon the ballots cast at said election shall be, ‘“Bonds, yes,” or

‘Bonds, no.”

Sec. 6. Upon the result of the said election being duly declared, if it shall
appear that the issuance of the said bonds is thereby authorized, the Council of the
said city may proceed, by resolution, to adopt and carry out such further measures
as shall be necessary to issue and sell the same for the purpose of fulfilling the object
of this ordinance hereinbefore specified.

Sxc. 7. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordinance,
and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily Heratb, and
thereupon and thereafter it shall be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of the
City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of April 14th, A. D. 1883.

RESOLUTION No. 133.

A Resotvrtton for the holding of a special election, at which shall be submitted to
a vote of the people, the question of issuing bonds to raise money to be used for
the purpose of purchasing a lot and erecting thereon public buildings for city
purposes,

Whereas, the City of Los Angeles has no public buildings in which the business
of the corporation can be transacted; and,


===== PDF PAGE 229 = PRINTED PAGE 228 =====
228 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  
  
   
  
  
  
 
  
  

Whereas, the cost of renting such accommodations as are absolutely necessary
for that purpose exceeds in amount the interest on a sum of money that would be
sufficient to purchase a lot and to erect thereon a handsome public edifice; and

Whereas, every consideration of economy and taste demand that the city should
erect and own such buildings as may be requisite and necessary for municipal
purposes; and,

Whereas, there are not sufficient funds in the treasury to purchase the land or
to erect such buildings; and,

Whereas, it is deemed expedient to issue six per cent. bonds, redeemable on ©
or before twenty years from the date of the issuance thereof, to the amount of not
exceeding one hundred thousand dollars, to raise money for the purpose above set
forth; and, i

Whereas, said bonds cannot be issued except by consent of the people, to be
expressed at a special election to be held for that purpose, now, therefore,

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles:

Section 1. That a special election be held in the City of Los Angeles, on
Thursday, the third day of May, A. D. 1883, at which shall be submitted to
the qualified voters of said city, the question of issuing six per cent. bonds of the
City of Los Angeles to the amount of not exceeding one hundred thousand dollars,
redeemable on or before twenty years from the date of the issuance thereof, for the
purpose of raising money with which to purchase a lot and to erect thereon suitable
buildings for the transaction of the municipal business, and to provide therein for
the arrangement and preservation of the records, papers and archives of said city.

Sec. 2, And it is further resolved, that the polling places for said election
shall be as follows:

For the First Ward, at Elite Sample Rooms, San Fernando street.

For the Second Ward, at the office of the Chief of Police, No. 31 Spring street.

For the Third Ward, at Turnverein Hall, Spring street.

For the Fourth Ward, at Engine House No. 2, Main street.

For the Fifth Ward, at the Pavilion, Washington Gardens, Washington street.

And it is further resolved:

Suc. 3. That the following-named persons, residents of the respective wards,
are hereby appointed to act respectively as Judges and Inspectors of said election,
to hold, conduct and make returns of said election; that is to say:

First Ward—Inspector, G. E. Long; Judges, J. M. Thomas and C. N. Earl.

Second Ward—Inspector, C. E. Parker; Judges, A. G. Mappa and 8. Moran,

Third Ward—Inspector, M. Teed; Judges, W. J. Neely and G. H. Pike.

Fourth Ward—Inspector, F. Sabichi; Judges, O. H. Bliss and Samuel Kutz.

Fifth Ward—Inspector, G. J. Clark; Judges, T. Leahy and J. T. Brown.

And be it further resolved,

Suc. 4. That the polls at said election shall be opened at one hour after sunrise
of said Thursday, the third day of May, A. D. 1883, and must be kept open until |
sunset, when the same must be closed.
