ORDINANCE No. 82.

Aw ORDINANCE relating to the running of engines, tenders and cars in the City
limits faster than six miles an hour, and providing for the punishment of those

violating its provisions.
The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Szction 1. It shall be unlawful for any locomotive engine, tender, car or train
of cars, driven or propelled by steam, to move in any direction within the limits of
the City of Los Angeles at a rate faster than six miles an hour.

Sec. 2. Any engineer, brakeman, driver, conductor or other person causing or
allowing any such locomotive, engine, tender, car or train of cars to move in any
direction within the limits of said city at.a rate faster than six miles an hour, shall,
upon conviction, pay a fine not less than fifty nor more than two hundred dollars, or
suffer imprisonment not less than fifty nor more than two hundred days, or both pay

said fine and suffer said imprisonment.

Szc. 3. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordinance,
and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily Hzratn,
and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of the
City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of May 19th, A. D. 1883.

duits, reservoirs and ditches, and relating to stealing water from companies and
persons supplying water to the inhabitants of the City of Los Angeles for do-

mestic purposes.
The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

Section 1. All persons are prohibited from breaking, tapping or in any way
injuring any water pipe, main, conduit, reservoir or ditch of any person or company

without the consent of such person or company.

Sec. 2. All persons are prohibited from using any water from any pipe, u
or hose connected with any service pipe through which water flows from any mal
conduit, reservoir or ditch of any person or company authorized to furnish and
furnishing the inhabitants of the City of Los Angeles with water for domestic 18%
without the consent of such person or company; but all the present or future officers

the authorities of the City of Los Angeles to change, alter or modify the grades of

ORDINANCE No. 84.

An ORDINANCE amending an ordinance entitled ‘‘An ordinance granting a franchise
for a street railroad in the City of Los Angeles to I. W. Hellman and his
assigns,” adopted September 9th, 1882, and approved September 20, 1882.

 

 

 

 

 


===== PDF PAGE 242 = PRINTED PAGE 241 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS. ANGELES. 241

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

Section 1. That the ordinance entitled “An ordinance granting a franchise
for a street railroad in the City of Los Angeles to I. W. Hellman and his assigns,”
adopted September 9th, 1882, and approved September 20th, 1882, is hereby amend-
ed, so that in addition to the franchise granted by the said ordinance, the right of
way be and the same is hereby granted to I. W. Hellman and his assigns, over and
along San Fernando street, in said city, for the period of thirty years from and after
the 20th day of September, 1882, for the purpose of laying down, maintaining and
operating one line of iron street railroad track, with the right to construct such
turnouts and switches as may be necessary to operate said road; said track shall be
what is commonly known as the ‘“‘broad gauge;” and the rails to be what are known
as ‘‘flat rails;” and to run cars thereon to be drawn or propelled by horses or mules;
that is to say: Commencing at the northern terminus, on San Fernando, of the right
of way granted by the said ordinance passed September 9th, 1882, and approved
September 20th, 1882, and extending two hundred and two feet northerly along
said San Fernando street, parallel to the easterly line of San Fernando street, to a
point opposite the north-west corner of San Fernando and Sotello streets.

The said route is more particularly delineated and shown in connection with
other railroad tracks and the sidewalks on the map, entitled ‘‘Map showing the pro-
posed route described in the application of I. W. Hellman for a franchise for a street
railroad,” which said map is on file in the office of the Clerk of the Council of the
City of Los Angeles.

Provided, and upon condition that the construction of said road shall be com-
menced within sixty days from and after the 19th day of May, 1883, and the whole
thereof shall be completed, equipped, stocked and in running order within two
years from said 20th day of September, 1882, it being understood that this franchise
shall be forfeited by the grantee, his heirs, successors or assigns herein, in case of a
failure to complete the said road within the said period of two years.

Provided further, and upon condition that the said grantee, or his heirs, succes-
sors and assigns, shall plank or pave or macadamize the entire length of said route
along which said road may be constructed, between the rails and for two feet on
either side thereof, and shall keep the same constantly in repair, flush with the
streets, and provided with crossings for all kinds of vehicles, and all necessary and
proper flumes and culverts for the free and uninterrupted passage of the water under
said track from lands higher than said track or road-bed is required to be, and the
track shall not be more than five feet between the rails, and there shall be a space
between the main tracks and side tracks or turnouts sufficient to allow the cars to
pass each other without danger; and provided further, that the laying of said track
shall conform in all cases, where any grade has been established, to such grade, and
in all other cases to the natural grade of the street through which it may run, and
when at any time any part of said route shall be graded, or the grade thereof
changed or altered, the bed of the road and the tracks thereof shall be made to eons
form therewith. And that no turnout nor switch shall be constructed, except in
places designated by the Council of the City of Los Angeles, nor shall they, in any
case, be placed nearer than one hundred feet from the junction of any two streets or
from any street crossing.


===== PDF PAGE 243 = PRINTED PAGE 242 =====
949 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

Provided further, and upon condition that at no time shall the rate of fare for
any distance along said road exceed the sum of five cents for one fare, and the owner
or owners shall pay each year such a license to said city upon each car as shall be
required by ordinance of said city.

Whenever any railroad track shall intersect this road, such road shall not occu-
py and use the track of this road for a greater distance than one block.

Sec. 2. It is understood that the city, in making the grant of this franchise,
expressly reserves the right to grade, renew, sewer, pave, macadamize, improve,
alter or repair all or either of said streets, or any part thereof, and to lay down
pipes for water, gas and other purposes, such work to be done by the city, so as to
obstruct or injure the road as little as possible, but when such work makes the same
necessary, the owner or owners of said road must shift the rails so as to avoid the
obstruction made thereby.

It is further understood that this franchise is especially granted upon all and
each of the provisoes and conditions herein contained.

And if such grantee, his heirs, successors or assigns shall fail in any particular
to comply therewith, or with either of them, then and in that case all rights to this
franchise shall be thereby forfeited and this grant shall be null and void, and that
nothing in this franchise shall be construed in any manner as granting an exclusive
franchise.

Src. 3. All ordinances and parts of ordinances in conflict with this ordinance
are hereby repealed. \ ‘

and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily Henan,
and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

RESOLUTION of intention to improve and grade Charity street, between First street
and Third street.

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles:

Section 1. That it is the intention of the Mayor and Council of the City of
Los Angeles to cause to be improyed and graded, at the expense of the property
owners, Charity street, between First street and Third street, in the following
manner:

The road-bed shall be graded and covered with eight inches of gravel, raked
free of coarse stones of more than two inches in diameter. The crown of the street
shall be nine inches above the grade, with such a slope toward the curb that at the
outside of the gutters it shall be six inches below the curb. After being graveled, it
shall be thoroughly wet and then rolled.

The gutters shall be 3} feet wide, concave at the bottom, and paved with
granite cobble. stones not less than twelve inches long and not more than six inches
in diameter, set upright in the sand, and thoroughly rammed to a smooth surface.
The center of the gutter shall be twelve inches, and the inside adjoining the curb
six inches below the grade.

The curb shall be of redwood, 3x12 inches, placed with the upper edge to the es-
tablished grade, and spiked to posts of redwood, 4x4 inches three feet long, set into
the ground full length below the top of the curb and inside of the same, and not
more than four feet apart, and one to each joint of the curbing.

The sidewalks shall be twelve feet wide, graded and covered with three inches

of fine gravel, smoothly laid and raked free of coarse stones of more than one inch in
diameter, The slope of the sidewalks shall be three inches toward the curb.

Szc. 2, That the exterior boundaries of the district of land to be affected or
benefited by said work or improvement, and to be assessed to pay the costs and
expenses thereof, are as follows:

ORDINANCE No. 87.

An ORDINANCE relating to the running of engines, tenders and cars in the city
limits of the City of Los Angeles, and providing for the punishment of those

violating its provisions.
The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

Szctton 1. It shall be unlawful for any locomotive, engine, tender, car or train
of cars driven or propelled by steam, to move in any direction within the limits of

the city of Los Angeles, between Kohler street and Downey Avenue, at a rate
faster than eight miles an hour.

Src, 2, Any engineer, driver, brakeman, conductor or other person, causing or
allowing any such locomotive, engine, tender, car or train of cars to move In any


===== PDF PAGE 253 = PRINTED PAGE 252 =====
252 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

direction within the limits of said city, between Kohler street and Downey Avenue,
at a rate faster than eight miles an hour, shall, upon conviction, pay a fine not legs
than fifty nor more than two hundred dollars, or suffer imprisonment not less than
fifty nor more than two hundred days, or both pay said fine and suffer said impris-

onment.

Sec. 3. All ordinances and parts of ordinances in conflict with this ordinance
are hereby repealed.

Src. 4. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordinance,
and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily Hxratp,

. ORDINANCE No. 89.

AN ORDINANCE granting franchise for street railroad to the Main Street and Agri-
cultural Park Railroad Company. .


===== PDF PAGE 257 = PRINTED PAGE 256 =====
256 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

Section 1. That the right of way be and the same is hereby granted to Main
Street and Agricultural Park Railroad Company, and to its assigns, over and along
the following streets of said city, until September 29th, 1894, for the purpose of
extending, laying, maintaining and operating one line of iron street railroad track,
with two parallel rails, distant from each other at least three feet, and to run cars
thereon to be drawn and propelled by horses or mules, and to carry passengers
thereon, with the privilege of constructing one turn-table at the easterly end thereof;
that is to say: j

Commencing at the present line of track of the Main Street and Agricaltural
Park Railroad, on the corner of Main and Washington streets, and running thence
in a straight line easterly along the center line of Washington street to a point five
hundred feet distant from the easterly boundary line of Main street; thence in a
straight line to the real property now owned by the Main Street and Agricultural
Park Railroad Company, on the corner of Washington and Carlisle streets.

Src. 2. The said line of road shall be completed within the period of four
months from and after the date of the taking effect of this ordinance.

Sec, 3. The laying of the track shall conform in all cases, where any part of
said route has been graded according to an established grade, to such established
grade, and in all other cases to the natural grade of the street through which it may
run; and when, at any time, any part of said route shall be graded, or the grade
thereof changed or altered, the bed of the road and the track thereof shall be made
to conform therewith.

Sec. 4. The said grantee and its assigns shall plank, pave or macadamize the
entire length of the street used by its tracks, between the rails and for two feet on
each side thereof, and shall keep the same constantly in repair, flush with the street,
and provided with good crossings, in length equal to the cross street in or opposite
which such crossing is made, and the track be not more than five feet wide within
the rails, and there be a space between the main tracks and side tracks or turnouts
sufficient to allow cars to pass each other freely and without danger.

Sec. 5. At no time shall any additional rate of fare be charged on said route,
but only the fare authorized to be charged for the road with which it is connected,

Sec. 6. It is expressly understood that the city of Los Angeles, in making the
grant of this franchise, expressly reserves the right to grade, sewer, pave, macad-
amize, improve, alter or repair all or either of said streets and any part thereof, and
to lay sewers or pipes for water, gas or other purposes therein; such work to be done
by the city so as to obstruct or injure the road as little as possible; but, when work
makes the same necessary, the owners of said road must shift the rails so as to
avoid the obstruction made thereby. It is further understood that this franchise is
specially granted upon all and each of the provisions and conditions herein con-
tained; and if the grantee or its assigns shall fail in any particular to comply there-
with, or with either of them, then, and in that case all right to this franchise shall


===== PDF PAGE 258 = PRINTED PAGE 257 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 257

be thereby forfeited and this grant be null and void, and that nothing herein con-
tained shall be construed in any manner as granting an exclusive franchise,

Sec. 7. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordinance,
and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily Hzratp,
and thereupon it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of the
City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of June 25th, A. D. 1883.

ORDINANCE No. 90.

Aw Ogpinance forbidding the obstruction of the streets of the City of Los Angeles,
providing for the placing of lamps upon building material in said streets, and
providing for the punishment of those violating its provisions.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. It is hereby declared unlawful for any person or persons, firm or
corporation to obstruct any street of the City of Los Angeles, by placing
building material therein, or otherwise, except by consent of the Council of said city;
and in case of the said consent having been obtained, any person placing building
material in such street, must proceed with the construction of the building for which
the said material is intended, with due diligence, and as rapidly as the weather, the
obtainable supply of workmen and material will allow, and remove the said material
with all possible dispatch considering the said circumstances. _

Szc. 2. Any person or persons, firm or corporation placing or causing to be
placed any of the said building material in said streets, shall swing two lighted lan-
terns, so provided and arranged as to burn fourteen hours, two feet from the ground,
at an half hour after sunset, and keep the same burning until'an half hour beforé
sunrise of each day. One lantern shall be placed at each end of said material.

Src. 3. Any person or persons, firm or corporation violating any of the pro-
visions of this ordinance, shall, upon conviction, pay a fine of not less than twenty-
five dollars, nor more than two hundred and fifty dollars, or be imprisoned not less
than twenty-five days, nor more than two hundred and fifty days, or both pay said

fine and suffer said imprisonment.
Sxc. 4. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordinance,

and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily Hunan,
and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

ORDINANCE No. 93.

An Orp1nance forbidding the obstruction of the streets of the City of Los Angeles
without the consent of the Council, providing for the placing of lamps upon
building material in said streets, and for the depositing of $25 with the Clerk of
the Council before obstructing said streets, and providing for the punishment of
those violating its provisions.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. Itis hereby declared unlawful for any person or persons, firm or
corporation to obstruct any street of the City of Los Angeles by placing building
material therein, or otherwise, except by consent of the Council of said city previ-
ously had and obtained, and unless a deposit of twenty-five dollars is first made
with the Clerk of the Council; provided, that in no case shall any part of any street
be obstructed at a greater distance than twenty feet from the sidewalk adjoining
which the building for which the said material is intended shall be constructed.
The said consent having been obtained, and the said deposit having been made, any
person placing building material in such street must proceed with the construction
of the building for which the said material is intended with due diligence, and as
rapidly as the weather and obtainable supply of workmen and material will allow,
and remove the said material and the debris thereof with all possible dispatch, con-

sidering the said circumstances.

Sxc. 2. Any person or persons, firm or corporation placing or causing to be
placed any of the said building material in said streets, shall swing two lighted
lanterns, so provided and arranged as to burn fourteen hours, two feet from the
ground, at an half hour after sunset, and keep the same burning until an half hour
before sunrise of each day. One lantern shall be placed at each end of said material.


===== PDF PAGE 279 = PRINTED PAGE 278 =====
278 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

Szc. 3. If every portion of the said building material and the debris thereof
shall not have been removed within three days after the completion of said building,
the Superintendent of Streets of the City of Los Angeles is hereby directed and
empowered to cause the removal of all said material and debris at the expense of the
person or persons, firm or corporation erecting said building or making said deposit,
and draw warrants on the Clerk of the Council, payable out of the said deposit, for
the work and labor done in removing said material and debris.

Sec. 4. Upon the production of a certificate from the Superintendent of Streets
that all said material and debris have been removed, the Clerk of the Council is
hereby directed and empowered to pay to the person, persons, firm or corporation
entitled thereto, the balance of the said twenty-five dollars remaining after paying
the said warrants.

Sec. 5. Any person or persons, firm or corporation violating any of the pro-
visions of this ordinance shall, upon conviction, pay a fine of not less than twenty -
five nor more than two hundred and fifty dollars, or be imprisoned not less than
twenty-five nor more than two hundred and fifty days, or both pay said fine and
suffer said imprisonment.

Sec. 6. All ordinances and parts of ordinances in conflict with this ordinance
are hereby repealed.

Src. 7. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordinance,

and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily Hrnratp,
and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.
I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of the
City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of August 4th, A. D. 1883.
W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles,

Approved this llth day of August, A. D. 1883.
C. E. THOM,

Mayor.
Published August 14th, 1883.

ORDINANCE No. 98.

An ORDINANCE prohibiting the defacing oi electric light poles and masts.
The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

Section 1. Any one defacing, marring or changing the appearance of any
painted electric light pole or mast in the City of Los Angeles, by posting any notice,
paper or advertisement thereon, or by painting, writing upon or coloring the same,
or in any other way, is guilty of a misdemeanor, and shall, upon conviction, pay a
fine of not less than five nor more than fifty dollars, or be imprisoned not less than
five nor more than fifty days, or both pay said fine and suffer said imprisonment.

ORDINANCE No. 99.

An ORDINANCE prohibiting the carrying of swill through the public streets during
certain hours.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

Section 1. The carrying of swill through the streets of the City of Los
Angeles, in any other manner than ina closed water-tight box, except between
the hours of § o’clock P. m. and 6 o’clock A. m., is hereby prohibited.

Sec. 2. The carrying of swill through the streets of the City of Los Angeles ,in
any water-tight box, except between the hours of 6 o’clock P. m. and 8 o’clock a. M.,
is hereby prohibited.

are hereby repealed.

ORDINANCE No. 100.

tection of life and property from fire and explosions, and regulating the erection
of buildings.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:


===== PDF PAGE 301 = PRINTED PAGE 300 =====
300 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

Secrion 1. That all that portion of the City of Los Angeles bounded and de-
scribed as follows, to-wit: commencing at the point of the intersection of Ninth and
Pearl streets, and running thence northerly along the middle line of Pearl street to
Canal and Reservoir street; thence along the middle line cof Canal and Reservoir
street south-westerly to Castellar street; thence northerly along the middle line of
Castellar street extended to the river Los Angeles; thence down the river Los
Angeles to the extension of Seventh street; thence westerly along the middle line of
the extension of Seventh street to San Pedro street; thence along the middle line of
San Pedro street southerly to Moran Lane; thence along the middle line of Moran
Lane north-westerly to Main street; thence westerly along the middle line of Ninth
street to the point of beginning, shall be the general fire limits of the City of Los

Angeles.

Sec. 2, That the general fire limits of the City of Los Angeles, as hereinbefore
established, shall be and the same are hereby divided into four districts, to be known
and designated respectively as District No. 1, as District No. 2, as District No. 3
and as District No. 4, of the general fire limits of the City of Los Angeles.

Sec. 3. The boundaries of the respective districts shall be as follows:

First—District No. 1 of the general fire limits of the City of Los Angeles shall
comprise and embrace all that portion of the general fire limits bounded and desig-
nated as follows, to-wit: Commencing at the intersection of the middle lines of
Alameda and Marchessault streets, and running thence southerly along the middle
line of Alameda street to Requena street; thence along the middle line of Requena
street westerly to a point 130 feet westerly from the west line of Wilmington street;
thence along a line parallel to the west line of Wilmington street southerly to the
middle line of Jackson street; thence along the middle line of Jackson street west-
erly to the middle line of Wilmington street; thence along the middle line of Wil-
mington street southerly to First street; thence along the middle line of First street
westerly to Los Angeles street; thence along the middle line of Los Angeles street
southerly to a point where an extension of the middle line of Second street would -
intersect said middle line of Los Angeles street; thence along said extension of the
middle line of Second street and the middle line of Second street westerly to Fort
street; thence along the middle line of Fort street northerly to Temple street; thence
along the middle line of Temple street easterly to New High street; thence along
the middle line of New High street to Marchessault street; thence along the middle
line of Marchessault street easterly to the place of beginning.

Suc. 4. It shall be and is unlawful for any person, persons, firm or corporation

Sec. 5. It shall be and is unlawful for any person or persons, firm or corpora-

limits of the city of Los Angeles.

Sec. 8. No person shall use any portable light in any building or place where
combustible materials or hay is kept, unless such light be securely kept in a
lantern.

Src. 9. Each person, firm or corporation making, using, or having charge or
control of shavings. hay, straw, sacks, bags, litter, or any other combustible waste
or fragments, shall remove all the same once in every two weeks.

Sec. 10. All warehouses used for storage of any kind of powder must be
located outside the general fire limits of the city of Los Angeles, and shall have
painted on the front of said warehouse, in plain Roman letters, the words ‘‘Storage
of Powder.”

Sec. 11. All buildings and all enlargements and alterations thereof hereafter
erected or made, and all enlargements and alterations hereafter made of all buildings
within the fire limits of Districts No. 1 and 3, of the general fire limits of the City
of Los Angeles, sha!l be made and constructed of brick, stone or iron, and every
building of brick, stone or iron, or both, that shall be newly roofed or covered, shall
be constructed with side walls or party walls of brick, stone or iron, or of both, and such
side walls and party walls shall extend from the foundation to the top of and through
the roof of the building, and said roof shall be covered with tin, iron, brick or stone.
Allside walls and party walls shall be so constructed as to separate all woodwork thor-
oughly and completely (of the interior and exterior of such buildings) from all and
every part of interior and exterior of every adjoining building; and every such side
wall or party wall shall pass through the roof of the building to which it may
appertain, in such a manner as to break entirely any communication of wood what-
ever between such roof and any other building. Every building sixty feet wide
hereafter erected in the said District No. 1, having a partition wall on the ground
floor, shall have at least one partition wall extending from the front to the rear of
the said building, and from the foundation and through as many stories as contain
one partition wall, to be constructed to the roof in the same manner as herein pro-
vided for side walls and party walls; every building eighty feet wide hereafter
erected in said District No. 1 having two partition walls on the ground floor shall
have two partition walls extending from the front to the rear of said building, and
from the foundation through as many stories of said building as contain two parti-
tion walls, to be constructed in the same manner as herein provided for side walls
and party walls; and for each additional twenty feet in width in every building
hereafter erected in said District No. 1 having partition walls on the ground floor, |
one additional partition wall shall be erected, extending from the front to the rear of
said building, and from the foundation and through as many stories as contain parti-
tion walls, to be constructed in the same manner as herein provided for side and
party walls. All partition walls shall be constructed as in this section provided.
All walls mentioned in this section shall be securely anchored with iron anchors; all
openings for doors and windows shall have a good and sufficient arch of stone or
brick, well built and keyed, or a lintel of stone or iron; no swelled or refuse brick
shall be allowed in any wall or pier; no mortar made of lime and sand shall be used
within twenty-four hours after being mixed; all sand shall be clean, sharp grit, free

Sec. 13. Ail foundation walls for buildings constructed of stone, brick or iron,
of more than one story in height, shall be built of stone or brick, and shall be laid
not less than three feet below the surface cf the earth, on a good, solid bottom;
bus in all cases every part of every foundation must rest on a good, solid
bottom. The footing or base course under all foundation walls of buildings of
stone, brick or iron shall be of stone or brick, and shall be at least twice the width
of the bottom course of the foundation walls, said footing course to be laid with five
courses of brick or the equal in height of the same of stone; and if the wails be built
of isolated piers, then there must be inverted arches at least twelve inches thick
turned under and between the piers, or two footing courses of large stone, at least
ten inches thick, im each course All foundation walls other than those of dwellings
shall be at least four inches thicker than the walls next above them to a depth of six-
teen feet below the curb level, as lawfully fixed, and shall be increased four inches in
thickness for every additional five feet in depth below said sixteen feet. Foundation
walls in dwellings shall be, below the basement flocr beams, four inches thicker than
the walls next above them. All foundation walls shall be understood to mean that
portion of the wall below the level of the street curb, and depth shall be computed
from the curb level downward. The depth of fourteen feet below the curb level of
the street is hereby fixed as the standard depth of foundations for brick and stone
buildings. Any person, firm or corporation excavating for or commencing founda-
tions at a greater depth than the above standard shall be responsible for all damages
to adjoining buildings, the foundations of which have been constructed at the
standard.

Src. 14. The outer walls of brick, stone or iron buildings are hereby declared
to be the front, rear and two side walls and the outer posts and pillars of said build-
ings, and in no case shall studding against brick walls be allowed.

Szc. 15. AM buildings hereafter erected within District No. 2 of the general
fire limits of the City of Los Angeles, except such as are intended to be and shall be
used exclusively as dwelling houses, and all alterations and enlargements of all
buildings in District No. 2, except such as are intended and are used exclusively as
dwelling houses, shall be made and constructed of brick, stone or iron, and in the
manner specified in section eleven hereof.

304 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

Src. 16. The outer walls of the upper stories in all buildings of stone, brick or
iron, or of both, to be used as dwelling houses, sheds, stables or other out-houses
hereafter to be erected in the City of Los Angeles, shall be at least eight inches in
- thickness; and the outer walls of all stories, except the upper, in all buildings
described in this section shall be at least twelve inches in thickness.

Szc. 17. The outer walls for all buildings of two stories, or less, to be used as
stores, warehouses, hotels, theaters and shops, shall be at least sixteen inches thick
in the basement or foundation, and twelve inches thick in the first and second
stories. In the outer walls for all buildings having three stories or less, the base-
ment shall be twenty inches thick, the first story seventeen inches thick, the
second and third stories twelve inches thick. For bvildings having four
stories, the walls of the basement or foundation must be twenty inches
thick, the walls of the first and second stories seventeen inches thick,
and the walls of the third and fourth stories twelve inches thick, The walls must be
of uniform thickness throughout the entire length of each wall. All party walls
must be twenty inches thick for basement or foundation, and sixteen inches thick
for each story, to the height of three stories above the basement or foundation, and
at least twelve inches thick to the top, so as to have four inches at least of solid
masonry between timbers. Party walls shall be understood to be solid brick or
stone walls, and shall be without openings.

Src. 18. All stone walls less than twenty-four inches shall have at least one
header extending through the walls in every six square feet, and if over twenty-four
inches in thickness shall have one header for every six superficial feet on both sides
of the wall and running into the wall at least two feet. In every brick wall every
fifth course of brick shall be a heading course, except where the walls are faced with
brick, in which case every fifth course shall be bound into the blocking by cutting
the courses of the faced brick and putting in diagonal headers behind the same, or
by splitting face brick in half and backing the same by a continuous row of headers,
In all walls which are faced with thin ashler anchored to the backing, or in which
the ashler has not either alternate headers and stretchers in each course, or alternate
heading and stretching courses, the backing of brick shall not be less than eight
inches thick, and all eight-inch backing shall be laid up in cement mortar, and shal]
not be built to a greater height than prescribed for eight-inch walls. All heading
courses shall be of good, hard, perfect brick.

Src. 19, All walls in brick, iron or stone buildings shall be securely anchored
with iron anchors to each tier of beams. ‘The front, rear, side, end and party walls
shall, if not carried up together, be anchored to each other every six feet in their
height by tie anchors made of one and three-quarter-inch by three-eighths of an inch
wrought iron. The said anchors shall be built into the front and rear walls at least
one-half the thickness of the front and rear walls, so as to secure the front and rear
walls to the side-end or party walls. And all stone used for the facing of any
building, except where built with alternate headers and ‘stretchers, as hereinbefore
set forth, shall be strongly anchored with iron anchors, and all such anchors shall be
let into the stone at least one inch. The side, end or party walls shall be anchored
to each tier of beams at intervals of not more than eight feet apart, with good,

‘strong wrought iron anchors, three-eighths of an inch by one and one-half inches
well built into the side walls, and well fastened into the sides of the beams; and
where the beams are supported by grinders the end of the beams resting on the
grinders shall be strapped by wrought iron straps of the same size, and at the same
distance apart, and in the same beams as the wall anchors. All wall anchors used
in any building shall be three-eighths by one and one-half inch wrought iron, and
shall hook over a three-quarter inch round bolt of wrought iron.

» Src. 20. In no building, whether the same be a frame building or otherwise,
shall any wooden beams or timber be placed within six inches of any flue, whether
the same be a smoke, air or any other flue. All wooden beams and other timbers in
the party wall of every building hereafter to be erected or built of stone, brick or
iron shall be separated from the beam or timber, but entering in the opposite side of
the wall by at least four inches of solid mason work. Every beam shall rest at each
end not less than four inches in the wall or upon a girder, as authorized by this

length, and such bond timbers shall be laid eighteen inches apart, parallel to each other,
and there shall be eighteen inches of brick or mason work between the ends of the
same. In all buildings where the floor beams are of wood, the ends of all beams
resting on the wall shall be cut to the level of three inches.

Src. 21. All openings for doors and windows in all buildings of brick, iron or
stone shall have a good and sufficient arch of stone or brick, well built and keyed,
and with good and sufficient abutments, or a lintel of stone or iron, as follows: For
an opening of not more than four feet in breadth, the lintels shall not be less than
eight inches in height; and for an opening of not more than five feet in breadth, the
lintels shall be twelve inches in height; and for an opening exceeding five feet in
breadth, the lintels shall increase in height over and above the twelve inches before
provided, one inch for every additional foot in breadth for the opening; and every
such opening less than five feet in breadth in all walls over eight inches in thickness
shall have a lintel of stone or iron not less than seven inches in breadth and one-
third the thickness of the wall on which it rests; and in all openings as aforesaid in
any eight-inch wall, the lintels shall be one-half the thickness of the wall; and on
the inside of all openings in which the lintels shall be less than the width of the
wall, there shall be a good timber lintel on the inside of the lintels, which shall rest
on each end not more than four inches on any wall, column, post or pillar, and shall
be chamfered at each end, and shall have a double rollock arch over the said lintel,
or the said arch may be turned on a center which may be struck after the arch is
turned; provided, the piers or abutments are of sufficient strength to bear the thrust
of the arch; and all arches over openings or fireplaces shall be built of good, hard
brick and well keyed; all lintels over openings returned on a corner building shall
be of iron or stone, of the height before provided for, and of the full thickness of the
wall to be supported; and where the second story window-sills rest upon the said
lintel course, the lintel shall be of iron or stone, and shall be the full size of the wall

Src. 22. No brick or stone wall shall be supported upon stringers of wood in
Districts Nos. 1, 2and 3 of the fire limits.

Sxc. 23. No person shall build a bay or oriel window which shall project over
the lines of any street, lane or alley more than three feet, nor be of a greater width
than eight feet, unless the bottom of such bay or oriel window is at least thirteen
feet in the clear above the sidewalk; provided, that no bay or oriel window shall be
built on any building fronting on any street, lane or alley which is less than thirty
feet in width; no swell front shall be built unless it be built as provided for bay or
oriel windows.

Src. 24. In all cases where hot water, steam, hot air or other furnaces are
used, the furnace smoke pipe must be kept at least two feet below the beams or
ceilings above the same, unless said beams or ceilings shall be properly protected by
a shield of tin plate suspeuded above said smoke pipe, with sufficient space for the
free circulation of air above and below said shield; and the smoke pipe shall in all
cases be kept at least eight inches from the beams and ceilings as aforesaid; and the
top of all furnaces set in brick must be covered with brick, slate or tin plate, sup-
ported by iron bars, and so constructed as to.be perfectly tight, said covering to be
in addition to and not less than six inches from the ordinary covering to the hot-air
chamber.

If, however, there is not height enough to build the furnace top at least four
inches below the floor beams or ceiling, then the floor beams must be trimmed around
the furnace, and said covering and trimmers and headers must be at least four inches
from the same. The top of portable furnace or furnaces not set in brick shall be
kept at least one foot below the beams or ceiling with a shield of tin plate made
tight and suspended below the said beams or ceiling, and extend one foot beyond
the top of the furnace or furnaces on all sides. All hot-air registers hereafter placed
in the floor of any building shall be set in soapstone borders not less than two inches
in width. All soapstone borders shall be firmly set in plaster of Paris or guaged
mortar; all floor register boxes shall be made of tin plate with a flange on the top to
fit the groove in the soapstone, the register to rest upon the same. There shall also
be an open space of two inches on all sides of the register-box, extending from the
under side of the ceiling below the registers to the soapstone in the floor; the outside
of the said space to be covered with a casing of tin plate made tight on all sides, and
shall extend from the under side of the aforesaid ceilings up to and turn under the
said soapstone. Registers twelve by nineteen inches, or less than fifteen by twenty-
five inches, shall have a space of three inches between register box and casing; regis-
ters of fifteen by twenty-five or more inches, shall have a space of three and a half
inches.

Sxc. 25. Whenever, in the judgment of the Committee on Fire and Water,

any cause whatever, be in a situation to be dangerous to persons or property, or

Src. 27. All the main aisles and passage-ways in buildings used for public

Src. 29. Spark catchers shall be placed upon all chimneys or smoke stacks

poses with benzine, naptha, gasoline or any other substance, and all oils from petro-
leum or its products shall stand a fire test of 110° Fahrenheit.

Src. 32. It shall be unlawful for any person to ignite, set fire to, or burn any
paper, shavings, boxes or other things upon any street, sidewalk or lots within the
limits of District No. 1 of the general fire limits, or ignite, set fire to, or burn any
paper, shavings, boxes or other things upon any street, sidewalk or lot within the
general fire limits, except between the hours of 6 a. m. and 8 A. M., or carry any

Src. 33, Any person, persons, firm or corporation who shall violate, neglect or
refuse to comply with any provision of this ordinance, shall be deemed guilty of a
misdemeanor, and on conviction thereof shall be fined not less than fifty dollars, nor
‘more than five hundred dollars, or be imprisoned in the jail not less than fifty days,
nor more than six months, or be both so fined and imprisoned. And every day
during which any building erected, altered or enlarged in violation of any of the
provisions of this ordinance continues in such condition, and every day during
which any violation of the ordinance continues, shall be considered as constituting
a new offence, and be punishable as in this section provided.

Szc. 34. All ordinances and parts of ordinances in conflict with the provisions
of this ordinance are hereby repealed.

ORDINANCE No. 101.

Aw ORDINANCE prohibiting the removal of sand and earth from the levee aligning
the Los Angeles river, and from any place without the official bed of the Los
Angeles river within 75 feet of the said official bed, and fixing the penalty for
the violation of its provisions.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

Section 1. Any person who shall remove any sand or earth from the levee
along and aligning the river bed of the Los Angeles river, or from any place without
the official bed of said river within 75 feet on either side of said official bed, shall be
deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and shall, on conviction, be punished by a fine of
not less than five nor more than one hundred dollars, or by imprisonment for not
less than five days, nor more than one hundred days, or by both such fine and
imprisonment.

Src. 2. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordinance,
and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily Hmratp,
and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of the
City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of September 29th, A. D. 1883.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Approved this 1st day of October, A. D. 1883.
Cc. E. THOM,

ORDINANCE No. 102.

An ORDINANCE of the City of Los Angeles defining the duties of the Health Officer,
fixing his remuneration, and repealing former ordinances and parts of ordinances.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

_ Secrion 1. No one shall be qualified for election to the office of Health Officer
for the City of Los Angeles who is not a resident practicing physician of said city,
a graduate of some reputable medical college, and who shall not have been adjudged
by the proper authorities to be entitled to practice medicine in the State of Cali-
fornia.

Sec. 2, The Health Officer shall devote all his time to his duties as such
officer; he shall keep an office in some convenient location, and shall keep the same
open for gratuitous vaccination during certain hours of each day, of which he shall
give public notice by advertisement from time to time in two newspapers, the one
English and the other Spanish; he shall give his personal attention and services to
the work of gratuitous vaccination, selecting and preserving the vaccine virus with
his utmost care and skill, and shall so perform his duties as to provide for the
physical well being of all who shall apply at his office; he shall attend upon and.
treat the city prisoners and inmates of the pest house, and perform such other duties
as the Board of Health of the City of Los Angeles shall require.

‘Src. 8. The Health Officer shall treat all cases of small pox, cholera and other
contagious diseases, in or out of the pest house, at any time, by night or by day,
when those suffering will accept his services.


===== PDF PAGE 313 = PRINTED PAGE 312 =====
col ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

Sec. 4. It shall be the duty of such Health Officer, and he is hereby authorized
and empowered, subject to the management and contrcl of said Board of Health, to
cause all the public streets, private lanes and alleys, houses, lots and premises
within the corporate limits of said city, whether public or private, and for whatever
purpose used or occupied, to be thoroughly cleaned and freed from all filth and
garbage in any way calculated to engender miasma or disease, to cause the same to
be thoroughly disinfected, so as to prevent the introduction, outbreak or spread of
any disease, whether contagious or otherwise; to visit personally and to inspect at
least once in every ten (10) days every portion and quarter of the city, including the
back yards and premises of the residences of the city; to notify, as hereinafter
directed, all parties whose premises are found to be in a filthy and unhealthy condi-—
tion, to clean the same and remove therefrom, within three days after the service of
notice upon them, whatever he may think is lable to produce any malarial or
contagious sickness; to see that the ordinances of the city relative to the prevention
and abatement of nuisances are rigidly enforced and carried out; and to make such
rules and regulations as he may think are demanded by the public safety for the
purpose of preventing at any time within the city of any disease or sickness, or the
spreading of any contagion or epidemic, and to enforce the same.

 

Src. 5. It shall be the duty of such health officer, upon finding for the first ~~

time any private premises within said city, in an unclean or unhealthy condition, to
give to the owner of such premises a notice in writing, to remove therefrom, within
three days, whatever he finds about or upon such premises calculated to produce
sickness or disease; and if at any time after such premises have been once ¢leared of
all filth and garbage, a second or any subsequent nuisance should be created thereon,
to give the occupant of such premises, whether he be the owner or lessee thereof, a
similar notice, and to the effect as aforesaid.

Src. 6. The Health officer of the City of Los Angeles is hereby authorized,
directed and empowered to notify all persons whose premises are found to beina —
filthy or unhealthy condition, to clean the same and remove therefrom immediately,
whatever is calculated or may be liable to produce disease.

Src. 7. The said Health Officer shall have the power at any time to call for
the assistance of the police force of the city to enforce a compliance with the pro-
visions of this ordinance, and with the rules and regulations by him made in pur-
suance hereof, and for the purpose of serving notices herein provided for and
required to be given.

Sec. 8. The Health Officer shall notify the Chief of Police of the City of Los
Angeles, of any neglect on the part of any policeman to the Health Officer, when he
shall observe that any building, street, alley, court, lot or premises in said city isn
a condition offensive to the public health.

Src. 9. Whenever a case of small-pox is reported to the Health Officer, it shall
be his duty, on proving the existence of the disease, to immediately cause to be
erected a yellow or quarantine flag in a conspicuous place on said premises, or to
have posted on the doorway of houses infected with the small-pox, a placard setting

 

 


===== PDF PAGE 314 = PRINTED PAGE 313 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 313

forth the fact, the same to remain during the continuance of the disease on said
premises.

Sec. 10. It shall be the duty of the Health Officer to keep a record of all
births, deaths and interments occurring in the City of Los Angeles in books duly
prepared for that purpose. Such records, when filled, shall be deposited in the

office of the Clerk of the Council, and produced, when required, for public
inspection.

Sec. 11. Said Health Officer may, with the consent of the Board of Health,
employ apy necessary number of assistants, and assign to each his duty, and deter-
mine their compensation, subject to the approval of the Council.

Sec. 12. It shall be the duty of the Health Officer of said city, when in the
opinion of the Board of Health it shall be deemed necessary for the health of the
city, to cause all and every train of cars, both passenger and freight, to be boarded
before the same shall enter the limits of said city, either by himself or some compe-
tent person appointed by him, and ascertain whether any person affected with small-
pox or varioloid or other contagious disease be on said train, and if any person so
affected shall be found thereon, it shall be the duty of the Health Officer, or the
person so appointed, to notify the conductor or person having charge of said train
thereof, and if, after such notice, the conductor or person having charge of said
train or trains, shall enter the limits of the city with said train or any part thereof,
until the permission of the health officer shall have been obtained, he shall be guilty
of a misdemeanor, and on conviction shall be punished by a fine of not less than one
hundred and fifty nor more than two hundred dollars, and imprisonment not less
than seventy nor more than ninety days. ;

Sec. 13. It shall be the duty of the Health Officer, when, in his opinion, he
deems it necessary for the health of the city, to notify the Superintendent, or the
person having charge of and control over any and all trains of cars entering in or
going out from said City of Los Angeles, to stop or cause all trains of cars, both
passenger and freight, to stop at some convenieut place (to be determined by the
Health Officer) ousside the limits of said city, before entering the same, and to
notify, or cause to be notified, by the posting of notices or otherwise, all conductors
or persons having charge of trains of cars entering in or going out from said city, to
stop with said train or trains before entering said city at the place so designated, so
that the same may be examined to see whether the same contain persons affected
with small-pox or varioloid or other contagious diseases.

Sec. 14. ‘The salary of the Health Officer shall be one hundred and fifty dollars
per month, as full compensation for all services rendered.

Sec. 15. All ordinances and parts of ordinances in conflict with this ordinance
are hereby repealed.

Sgc. 16. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordinance,
and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily HERALD,
and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

Los Angeles, to cause to be improved and graded, at the expense of the property
owners, the extension of Bunker Hill avenue, between Temple street and Montreal
street in the following manner:

The road-bed shall be graded and covered with eight inches of gravel, raked
free of coarse stones of more than two inches in diameter, and it shall be made to
conform to the established grade at the center of the street, with the proper slope
toward the curb. After being graveled, it shall be thoroughly wet and then rolled

The curb shall be of redwood, 3x12 inches, placed with the upper edge to the
established grade and spiked to posts of redwood, 4x4 inches 3 feet long, set full
length in the ground below the top of the curb and inside of the same, and not more
than four feet apart, and one to each joint of the curbing.

The gutters shall be three feet wide, concave at the bottom, and paved with
granite cobble stones not less than 12 inches long and not more than 6 inches in
diameter, thoroughly set in sand and then rammed. The center of the gutter shall
be 12 inches and the outer edge shall be 6 inches below the grade.

The sidewalks shall be eight feet wide, graded and covered with three inches
of fine gravel, smoothly laid and raked free of coarse stones of more than one inch in
diameter. The slope of the sidewalk shall be three inches toward the curb.

Sec. 2. That the exterior boundaries of the district of land to be affected or
benefited by said work or improvement, and to be assessed to pay the costs and ex-
penses thereof, are as follows:

Commencing at the point of intersection of the center line of Bunker Hill
avenue extension and the northerly boundary of Temple street, and running thence
along the northerly boundary of Temple street westerly 100 feet; thence on a line
parallel to the center line of Bunker Hill avenue extension northerly 435 feet;
thence on the north line of Sand street produced westerly, easterly 200 feet; thence
‘on a line parallel to the center line of Bunker Hill avenue extension southerly 435
feet; thence westerly 100 feet to the point of beginning.

ORDINANCE No. 106.

An ORDINANCE granting a franchise for a street railroad in the City of Los Angeles,
to the Central Railroad Company.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

Section 1. That the reasonable right of way be and the same is hereby granted
to the Central Railroad Company, over and along the following-named public streets
of said city, for the period of twenty years from and after the date of the passage of
this ordinance, for the purpose of laying down, operating and maintaining one line
of street railroad track and all necessary turnouts and switches, with two parallel
iron rails, and to run cars thereon to be propelled by horses or mules, and to carry
passengers thereon, as follows:

Commencing at a point on Aliso avenue, at or near Chicago street; thence along
Chicago street by any course adopted and acquired by the Central Railroad Company
across block K, subdivision of lot 6, block 60, Hancock’s survey of said city, ac-
cording to the map thereof recorded in the office of the Recorder of Los Angeles
county, made by Moore and Kelleher; thence along Aliso avenue extension to Hver-
green Cemetery; and thence to the eastern extremity of said city, with all the nec-
essary turnouts and switches of said Central Railroad Company to depots located on
said street or terminus.

Provided, further, and upon condition that the said grantee or its assigns shall
plank or pave the entire route along which said road may be constructed between
the rails and for two feet on each side thereof, at all times whenever ordered to do so
by the Council of the city of Los Angeles, or by that body, person or persons who
may, by operation of law succeed to the rights, duties or privileges of the Council of
the city of Los Angeles; and shall keep the same and all tracks and all portions of
the said streets over which any part of said track may be constructed, between the


===== PDF PAGE 335 = PRINTED PAGE 334 =====
334 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

rails and for two feet on each side thereof, constantly in repair, flush with the streets,
and provided with good crossings for all kinds of vehicles, and with all necessary
and proper flumes and culverts for the free and uninterrupted passage of the water
under said track from lands higher than said track or road-bed is required to be,
whenever and wherever the Council of Los Angeles city or the successors of said
Council shall order the said flumes and culverts to be placed; and the track be not
more than five feet wide between the rails, and there be a space between the main
track and side tracks or turn-outs sufficient to allow the cars to pass each other
freely and without danger.

Provided further, that all curves made in the construction of this road shall be
designated and laid out by the City Surveyor of the City of Los Angeles; and pro-
vided further, that the laying of said track shall conform in all cases, where any
grade has been established, to such established grade, and in all other cases to the.
natural grade of the street through which it may run; and when, at any time, any
part of said route shall be graded, or the grade thereof changed or altered, the bed
of the road and the track thereof shall be made to conform therewith. Provided,
and upon condition that the construction of said road shall be commenced within
six months from and after the date of the taking effect of this ordinance, and the
whole thereof shall be completed and in running order within one year from and
after the said date of the taking effect of this ordinance.

Src. 2. That whenever any other track shall intersect this road, such road in
no case shall occupy and use a track of this road for a distance of more than ten
blocks; and if the owners of such intersecting tracks cannot agree upon the amount
of compensation to be made therefor, the same may be ascertained and determined
as provided in title VII, part ITI, Code of Civil Procedure, with amendments
thereto.

Sec. 3. Provided further, and upon condition that at no time shall the rate of
fare for any distance along said road and along those street railroads constructed in
pursuance and by virtue of the franchise granted to William H. Workman and A.
H. Judson, on January 29th, 1875, and the franchise granted to the Los Angeles
and Aliso Avenue Street Railroad Company, approved October 3, 1877, exceed the
sum of five cents.

Ssc. 4. That the owner or owners of said road shall pay, on the first Monday
of December of each year, a license to the city of Los Angeles upon each car belong-
ing to or used by said Central Railway Company, as may be required by ordinance
of said city.

Sxc. 5. And provided that the laying down of the tracks of the said road
shall, in all respects conform to the grade of said streets established and regulated
by said city, which is to be designated by the City Surveyor to the engineer of the
road at the time of laying the tracks, but subject to the reservations, provisions and
conditions herein contained.

Sec. 6. That the city, in making the grant of this franchise, reserves the right
to grade, renew, sewer, pave, macadamize, improve, alter or repair either of said
streets or any part thereof throughout the whole length of said road, and to lay

 


===== PDF PAGE 336 = PRINTED PAGE 335 =====

down pipes for water, gas and other purposes therein, such work to be done by the
city so as to obstruct the road as little as possible, and when work or need for work
makes the same necessary, the owner or owners must shift the rails so as to avoid
the obstructions made thereby. And, provided further, that this franchise is
especially granted upon all and each of the provisions, provisos and conditions herein
contained and reserved; and if the said grantee or its successors or assigns shall fai]
in any particular to comply therewith or with either of them, or shall fail for the
period of six months or longer to operate, maintain and use the street railroad built
by virtue of this franchise, all rights to this franchise hereby granted shall be thereby
forfeited, and this grant shall be null and void. And provided further, that nothing
herein contained shall be construed as granting any exclusive franchise in said streets,
and all turn-tables are prohibited.

in conflict herewith are hereby repealed.

RESOLUTION No. 205. |

RESOLUTION ordering the grading and improvement of Second street, between Main
and Fort streets.

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles:

Section 1. That there be and hereby is ordered to be graded and improved, at
the expense of the property owners within the district of land described in section 2

of this resolution, Second street, between Main and Fort streets, in the following
manner:

The road-bed shall be graded and covered with eight inches of pravel, raked
free of coarse stones of more than two inches in diameter, and it shall be made to
conform to the established grade at the center of the street, with the proper slope
toward the curb. After being graveled, it shall be thoroughly wet and then rolled.

The curb shall be of redwood, 3x12 inches, placed with the upper edge to the
established grade and spiked to posts of redwood, 4x4 inches three feet long, and set
into the ground full length below the top of the curb and inside of the same, and
not more than four feet apart, and one to each joint of the curbing.

The sidewalks shall be ten feet wide, graded and covered with three inches of
fine gravel, smoothly laid and raked free of coarse stones of more than once inch
in diameter. The slope of the sidewalk shall be three inches toward the curb.

Src. 2. That the exterior boundaries of the district of land to be affected or
benefited by said work or improvement, and to be assessed to pay the costs and
expenses thereof, are as follows:

Commencing at the point of intersection of the east boundary of Fort street
with the center line of Second street, and running thence southerly 100 feet;
thence on a line parallel to the center line of Second street easterly 740 feet to
the west boundary of Main street northerly 200 feet; thence on a line parallel to
the center line of Second street, westerly 740 feet, to the east boundary of Fort
street; thence southerly 100 feet to the point of beginning.

Sec. 3. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this resolution,
and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily HERatp,
and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing resolution was adopted by the Council of the
City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of November 24th, A. D. 1883.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Approved this 26th day of November, A. D. 1883.

with the west boundary of Cemetery avenue, and running thence along the west.
boundary of Cemetery avenue southerly 100 feet to a point; thence on a line parallel
to the center line of Sand street westerly 1234.6 feet to a point; thence northerly
200 feet to a point; thence on a line parallel to the center line of Sand street
easterly 1234.6 feet to the west boundary of Cemetery avenue; thence southerly
100 feet to the point of beginning.

Sec. 3. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this resolution,

An Onprnance granting a franchise for a street railroad in the City of Los Angeles
to the Central Railway Company.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

Secrion 1. That the reasonable right of way be and the same hereby is

350 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

granted to the Central Railway Company over and along the following-named public
streets of said city for the period of twenty years from and after the date of the
passage of this ordinance, for the purpose of laying down, operating and maintaining
one line of street railroad track and all necessary turnouts and switches, with two
parallel iron rails, and to run cars thereon to be propelled by horses or mules, and to
carry passengers thereon, as follows:

Commencing at a point on Aliso avenue. at or near Chicago street; thence along
Chicago street or by any course adopted and acquired by the said Central Railway
Company across block K, subdivision of lot 6, block 60, Hancock’s survey of said
city, according to map thereof recorded in the office of the Recorder of Los Angeles
county, made by Moore and Kelleher; thence along Aliso avenue extension to Ever-
green Cemetery; and thence to the eastern extremity of said city, with all the neces-
sary turnouts and switches of said Central Railway Company to depots located on
said street or terminus.

Provided further, and upon condition that the said grantee or its assigns shall
plank or pave the entire route along which said road may be constructed, between the
rails and for two feet on each side thereof, at all times whenever ordered to do so by the
Council of the city of Los Angeles, or by that body, person or persons who may, by
operation of law, succeed to the rights, duties or privileges of the Council of the city of
Los Angeles; and shall keep the same and all tracks and all portions of the said
streets over which any part of said track may be constructed, between the rails and
for two feet on each side thereof constantly in repair, flush with the streets, and pro-
vided with good crossings for all kinds of vehicles, and with all and proper neces-
sary flumes and culverts for the free and uninterrupted passage of the water under
said track from lands higher than said track or road-bed is required to be, whenever
and wherever the Council of Los Angeles city or the successors of said Council shall
order the said flumes and culverts to be placed, and the track be not more than five
feet wide between the rails, and there bea space between the main track and the
side tracks or turnouts sufficient to allow the cars to pass each other freely and with-
out danger; and provided, further, that all curves made in the construction of this
road shall be designated and laid out by the City Surveyor of the city of Los
Angeles; and provided, further, that the laying of said track shall conform in all
cases where any grade has been established to such established grade, and in all
other cases to the natural grade of the street through which it may run; and when
at any time any part of said route shall be graded, or the grade thereof changed or
altered, the bed of the road and the track thereof shall be made to conform there-
with. Provided, and upon condition that the construction of said road shail be com-
menced within six months from and after the date of the taking effect of this ordi-
nance, and the whole thereof shall be completed and in running order within one
year from and after the said date of the taking effect of this ordinance.

Szc. 2. That whenever any other track shall intersect this road, such road in
no case shall occupy and use a track of this road fora distance of more than five
blocks; and if the owners of such intersecting tracks cannot agree upon the amount
of compensation to be made therefor, the same may be ascertained and determined
as provided in Title VII, Part III, Code of Civil Procedure, with amendments
thereto.

ORDINANCE No. 112.

An ORDINANCE granting a franchise for a street railroad in the City of Los Angeles,
to I. W. Hellman and his assigns.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows;

Section 1. That the reasonable right of way be and the same is hereby granted
to I. W. Hellman, and to his assigns, over and along the following-named public
streets of said city, for the period of twenty-nine years from and after the 20th day
of September, A. D. 1883, for the purpose of laying down, maintaining and operating
one line of iron or steel street railroad track, with its necessary turn-outs and
switches, to be what is commonly known as the broad gauge, and the rails to be
what are known as flat rails, and to run cars thereon to be drawn or propelled by.
horses or mules; that is to say:

Commencing at a point op the center line of the track of the City Railway
Company, as now constructed, said point being located seventy feet south-westerly
-from the northerly boundary of Sotello street produced westerly, and running thence
on a curve with a radius of forty-five feet easterly to the center line of Sotello street;
thence along the middle of Sotello street easterly to the intersection of Sotello
_and Chavez streets; thence along Chavez street, and crossing the Los Angeles river
on said street, north-easterly to the intersection of Chavez and Chestnut streets;
thence along Chestnut street north-westerly to the intersection of Chestnut and Hoff
streets; thence along Hoff street north-easterly to the intersection of Hoff and Daly
streets; thence along Daly street southerly to the north boundary of Downey avenue.

And, also, the right to construct such turn-outs, sidings, switches and curves as
may be necessary to operate said road; provided, that all curves whose total curva-
ture shall exceed sixty degrees shall have radii not to exceed forty-five feet in
length. Provided, and upon condition that one mile of said road shall be fully
completed, equipped, stocked and in running order within the period of one year
from said 20th day of September, A. D. 1883, and the whole thereof shall be com-
pleted and in running order within two years from said 20th day of September, A.
D. 1883, it being understood that this franchise shall be forfeited by the grantee
herein on account of a failure to complete the said road within the said period of
two years.

_ After complying with the conditions and terms of this franchise, the said I. W.

 


===== PDF PAGE 358 = PRINTED PAGE 357 =====
OF THE OITY OF LOS ANGELES. 357

“Hellman, or his assigns, at any time during the period of twenty-nine years from
and after the 20th day of September, A. D. 1883, shall have the right should he or
they so elect, to lay down and operate upon the streets above and herein mentioned,

_ adouble track of like gauge and class of rail, and in the same manner required by
- this ordinance regarding the single track.

Provided further, and upon condition that the said grantee or heirs shall plank
or pave the entire length of said route along which said road may be constructed,
between the rails and for two feet on each side thereof, whenever ordered to do so
by the Council of the City of Los Angeles, or by that body, person or persons who
may, by operation of law, succeed to the rights, duties or privileges of the Council
of the City of Los Angeles, and shall keep the same and all portions of the said
streets over which any part of said track may be constructed, between the rails and
for two feet on each side thereof, constantly in repair, flush with the streets, and
provided with good crossings for all kinds of vehicles, and with all necessary and
proper flumes and culverts for the freeand uninterrupted passage of the water under
said track from lands higher than said track or road-bed is required to be, whenever
and wherever the Council of the City of Los Angeles or the successors of said Coun-
cil shall order the said flumes or culverts to be placed, and the track be not more
than five feet between the rails, and there be a space between the main tracks and
side tracks or turn outs sufficient to allow the cars to pass each other freely and
without danger; provided further, that all curves made in the construction of this
road shall be designated and laid out by the City Surveyor of the City of Los
Angeles; and provided further, that the laying of said tracks shall conform in all
cases when any grade has been established to such established grade, and in all other
eases to the natural grade of the street through which they may run; and when at
any time any part of said route shall be graded, or the grade thereof changed or
altered, the bed of the road and the tracks thereof shall be made to conform
therewith.

And that whenever any other track shall intersect this road, such road in no
case shall occupy and use a track of this road for a distance of more than ten blocks,
and if the owners of such intersecting tract cannot agree upon the amount of com-
pensation to be made therefor, the same may be determined as provided in Title
VII, Part III, Code of Civil Procedure, with amendments thereto.

Provided further, and upon condition that at no time shall the rate of fare for
any distance along said road and along those street railroads constructed in pur-
suance and by virtue of the franchises granted to I. W. Hellman and his assigns by
ordinances approved September 20th, 1882, September 4th, 1883, and May 28th,
1883, respectively, exceed the sum of five cents for one fare; and the owner or own-
ers thereof shall pay on the first day of December of each year such a license to said
city upon each car as may be required by ordinance of said city.

Provided further, and upon condition that if at any time for the space of six
months the said road or any portion thereof be unused by the said I. W. Hellman
or his assigns as a street railroad, the franchise for the said portion so unused shall

_ be thereby forfeited.

Src. 2, It is understood that the city, in making the grant of this franchise,
expressly reserves the right to grade, renew, sewer, pave, macadamize, improve,

alter or repair all or either of said streets or any part thereof throughout the whole |
length of said road, and to lay down pipes for water, gas and other purposes; such

work to be done by the city so as to obstruct or injure the road as little as possible;

>
but, when work makes the same necessary, the owner or owners of said road must

shift the rails so as to avoid the obstruction made thereby.

It is further understood that this franchise is especially granted upon each and
all of the provisions and conditions herein contained and reserved, and if said grantee
or his successors in interest or assigns shall fail in any particular to comply there-
with, or with either of them, then and in that case all rights to this franchise shall

be thereby forfeited, and this grant shall be null and void; and that nothing herein —

contained shall be construed in any manner as granting an exclusive franchise.

Sec. 3. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordinance,
and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily Heratp,
a newspaper published in said city, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect
and be in force.

City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of December 8th, A. D. 1883.

ORDINANCE No. 113.

AN Orpinance forbidding all persons, without a permit, to open or dig up any of
the streets of the city of Los Angeles.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles do ordain as follows:

Secrion 1. It shall be unlawful for any person or persons to open, dig up, €x-
cavate or in any manner injure by digging or excavating, any of the public streets
of the city of Los Angeles, without a written permit, signed by the Superintendent
of Streets of the city of Los Angeles so to do.

Sec. 2. The Superintendent of Streets shall issue no permit for sewer connec
tions without an order of the Council of said city, or of the Committee on Sewers of
said Council to that effect, and all sewer connections shall be made under the super-
vision of the Superintendent of Streets, and in case of permit for sewer connection
on graded streets, the Superintendent of streets shall require the deposit of the sum
of twenty dollars, to be returned when the street is placed in as good order as
found.

Src. 3. The provisions hereof shall apply to all persons or corporations, wheth-
er acting under a charter or right heretofore granted or not, and no excavation shall

j

 


===== PDF PAGE 360 = PRINTED PAGE 359 =====
re

wate
ay

OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 359

hereafter be made in any of the streets of said city for the purpose of laying down
any pipe.to conduct water, gas, sewarage or any other substance, nor shall any pipe
be laid down at all, or any excavations whatever made, without permission herein
provided for first having been obtained.

. Src. 4. All persons violating any of the provisions of this ordinaece shall be
guilty of a misdemeanor, and shall be fined in a sum not less than ten dollars and
not more than three hundred dollars.

SEc. 5. All ordinances and parts of ordinances, in so far as they conflict with
this ordinance, are hereby repealed.

Sec. 6. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordinance,
and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily HERap,
and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of the
City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of the 7th day of January, A. D. 1884.

W. W. ROBINSON,
