RESOLUTION No. 219.

RESOLUTION ordering the payment for the construction of section 4 of the Hill and

Seventh streets Sewer.

Be it resolved by the Mayor ard Council of the City of Los Angeles:

Section 1. The City-Treasurer of the city of Los Angeles is hereby directed
to pay out of Hill and Seventh Streets sewer fund, at the expiration of fifteen days
after the passage of this resolution, to Jos. H. Smith, the contractor for the construc-
tion of section four of the above named sewer, the sum of six hundred and _ six-
teen dollars and fifty cents ($615.50).

Provided, however, that said payment by the Treasurer shall be made subject
to the following provisions, to-wit: that any person or persons who have performed
labor upon, or furnished material for the construction of said work or improvement,
may file within the said fifteen (15) days with the City Treasurer of Los Angeles city,
any written claim or claims he or they may make, on account of such labor per-
formed, or material furnished; and at the expiration of said fifteen days said City
Treasurer shall pay to said contractor the amount specified in this resolution, less
the aggregate amount of all such claims, if any filed, in accordance with the provis-
ions of Section 15 of ‘‘an act for the improvement oi streets, lanes, courts, places
and sidewalks, and the construction of sewers within municipalties,” approved
March 6, 1883.

Should any money be retained by said Treasurer on account of any such claim
or claims, he shall pay over the amount of each claim only upon the order therefor
of said contractor, endorsed by claimant therefor, or upon the order therefor of
any Court of competent jurisdiction.

Sc, 2. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this resolution,
and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily Hrrato,

RESOLUTION No. 220.

RESOLUTION of the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, to establish the
grade of Court House street from Hope street to Flower street.

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles:

Section 1, That the grade of Court House street, from Hope street to Flower
street, be and the same is hereby established as follows:

At the north-east corner of Hope and Court House streets the grade shall be, as
now established, 137 feet above the datum plane; at the north-west corner of Hope
and Court House streets the grade shall be, as now established, 139 feet above the
datum plane; at the south-east corner of Hope and Court House streets the grade
shall be, as now established, 140 feet above the datum plane, and at the south-west
corner of Hope and Court House streets the grade shall be, as now established, 142
feet above the datum plane; at a point in the center line of Court House street, 165
feet westerly from the west boundary of Hope street, the grade shall be, on the
south side of Court House street, 154 feet above the datum plane, and on the north
side of Court House street, 152 feet above the datum plane; at the north-east cor-
ner of Court House and Flower streets the grade shall be 140.50 feet above the da-
tum plane, and at the south-east corner of Court House and Flower streets the grade
shall be 142.50 feet above the datum plane.

Szc. 2. The Clerk of the Council shail certify to the passage of this resolution,
and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily Heraxp,
and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of the 7th day of January, A. D. 1884.

RESOLUTION No. 221.

Rersoturion of intention to improve and grade Buena Vista street from Short street
to High street.
Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles as follows:

Sucrron 1. That it is the intention of the Mayor and Council of the city of
Los Angeles to cause to be improved and graded, at the expense of the ‘property

owners, Buena Vista street, from Short street to High street, in the following

manner: : ;
The road-bed shall be graded and covered with eight inches of gravel, raked

free of coarse stones of more than two inches in diameter, and it shall be made to


===== PDF PAGE 363 = PRINTED PAGE 362 =====
362 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

conform *to the established grade at the center of the street, with the proper slope
toward the curb. After being ‘graveled, it shall be thoroughly wet and then
rolled.

The curb shall be of redwood, 3x12 inches, placed with the upper edge to the
established grade and spiked to posts of redwood, 4x4 inches 3 feet long, set into
the ground full length below the top of the curb and inside of the same, and not more
than four feet apart, and one to each joint of the curbing.

The sidewalks shall be twelve feet wide, graded and covered with three inches
of fine gravel, smoothly laid and raked free of coarse stones of more than one inch in
diameter. The slope of the sidewalk shall be three inches toward the curb.

Src. 2. That the exterior boundaries of the district of land to be affected or
benefited by said work or improvement, and to be assessed to pay the costs and ex-
penses thereof, are as follows:

Commencing at the point of intersection of the center line of Buena Vista street
with the north boundary of High street, and running thence along the north bound-
ary of High street westerly 100 feet; thence on a line parallel to the center line of
Buena Vista street southerly 720 feet to the south boundary of Short street; thence
along the south boundary of Short street easterly 200 feet; thence on a line parallel
to the center line of Buena Vista street northerly 720 feet to the north boundary of
High street; thence westerly 100 feet to the point of beginning.

Src. 3. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this resolution,
and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily H=RaLp,
and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of January 7th, A. D. 1884.

W. W. ROBINSON,
